sourceContent.headline: AI agents are changing what CPU performance means
sourceContent.description: Discover how AI agents are reshaping CPU performance, placing greater importance on orchestration, memory, I/O, and sustained system efficiency.
paragraphs: On OpenRouter, agent token usage has increased roughly 14x since February 2026, according to data highlighted by a16z .

As Agentic AI is changes the unit of scale in the data center - he'll explore why scaling this shift depends on open, interoperable infrastructure built for performance and Meet @amazon's first-ever lineup of Alexa tablets!

📱 Built on Arm, the flagship 12 Pro features the @MediaTek Dimensity 8400 with Arm Cortex-A725 CPUs and Mali-G720 graphics, delivering performance and power efficiency for everyday experiences. 10 years of micro:bit!

AI agents are still early, but their activity is growing fast. On OpenRouter, agent token usage has increased roughly 14x since February 2026, according to data highlighted by a16z . From an infrastructure perspective, an AI agent behaves like a virtual user with its own persistent compute environment – maintaining state, retrieving context, invoking tools and services, executing work and evaluating results until a task is complete.

Now multiply that across millions or even billions of agents running 24×7. Compute, memory, storage and I/O all have to support continuous activity at high concurrency. That puts new demands on the CPU – and creates a need to measure how well systems handle the work agents actually complete.

Agentic AI creates compute demand across multiple parts of the AI data center. CPUs execute agent workloads as they maintain context, call tools and access data. At the AI head node, CPUs schedule work, prepare and move data, and coordinate the system to keep expensive accelerators productive.

articles.title: Non-custodial wallets' growing prevalence calls for investor protection
articles.titleEn: Non-custodial wallets' growing prevalence calls for investor protection
summaryLinesEn: However, with NCWs likely to gain prevalence as their UIs continue to get userfriendlier, the current absence of investor protection for NCW users is a concern.
Trading cryptoassets using a non-custodial (aka self-custody) wallet is currently outside the purview of Japan’s crypto regulations.
Japan would be well advised to look more deeply into providing such protection instead of leaving NCW users to fend for themselves.

summaryLinesEn: Online services now require multilayer defenses encompassing security precautions designed into the services from the outset, dynamic anomaly detection and cyber business continuity planning to ensure resilience against emerging threats.
Sophisticated forgeries are increasingly being used to bypass eKYC authentication processes, while phishing sites can now be created and deployed at unprecedented speed and scale.
As a result, organizations must strengthen defenses against the exploitation of vulnerabilities and loopholes in system specifications.

As part of Nomura Research Institute's (NRI) INSIGHT SIGNAL initiative, NRI conducts regular surveys of consumers across Tokyo and the six surrounding prefectures to support marketing consulting, public policy recommendations, and information sharing. The research continuously analyzes how current events and emerging trends influence consumer behavior. As part of these efforts, this article focuses on “ New Sports ” and “ Eatertainment ”, new forms of sports and leisure that have been attracting growing attention overseas. The survey explores how consumers perceive these emerging experiences and what values and expectations they associate with them.

People's engagement with sports has expanded beyond simply participating to include a variety of other forms, such as watching sports. Figure 1 illustrates consumers' favorability toward playing sports and watching sports . (Respondents were asked to rate each on a four-point scale: "Like," "Somewhat like," "Somewhat dislike," and "Dislike." The chart shows the combined percentage of respondents selecting "Like" or "Somewhat like.")

Source: NRI INSIGHT SIGNAL Survey (Residents aged 15–69 in Tokyo and six surrounding prefectures, June 2026, N = 3,018) Respondents rated each item on a four-point scale ("Like," "Somewhat like," "Somewhat dislike," and "Dislike"). The chart shows the combined percentage of those who responded "Like" or "Somewhat like."

articles.titleEn: Overview of Fermentation: Expanding Market Potential and Business Opportunities
summaryLinesEn: As these areas are expected to experience rapid growth, understanding how to evaluate their market potential and identify business opportunities will become increasingly important in assessing the overall fermentation industry.

At the same time, rising interest in gut health has accelerated demand for probiotics, and dairy products such as yogurt that contain live beneficial microorganisms are expected to continue supporting market growth.

It also examines key trends in the fermentation market, highlights important market developments, explores how fermentation can help address social challenges, and discusses business opportunities arising from fermentation, along with recommendations for future initiatives.

paragraphs: As these areas are expected to experience rapid growth, understanding how to evaluate their market potential and identify business opportunities will become increasingly important in assessing the overall fermentation industry.

This report provides a systematic overview of what fermentation is by organizing its definitions and various perspectives while introducing the potential of fermentation as an increasingly familiar part of everyday life, not only through fermented foods, but also through its broader applications.

Fermentation is a biological process in which microorganisms such as molds, yeasts, and bacteria, break down and synthesize organic compounds, including carbohydrates and proteins, resulting in chemical transformations. Because these processes produce outcomes that are beneficial to humans, such as improved preservation, enhanced nutritional value, and richer flavor, fermentation has long been utilized in everyday life. In contrast, putrefaction also results from the activity of microorganisms but produces substances that are harmful or undesirable to humans.

sourceContent.headline: Claude discovers a novel enzyme system
sourceContent.description: In early results from our new life sciences research lab, Claude agents found an enzyme system whose function is still unknown.
paragraphs: After 21 hours spent searching this data by roughly 950 agents using 210 million tokens, one of the agents spotted something remarkable: a repeating pattern of DNA sequences that occurs next to the gene for an odd-looking RT.

Our research prior to joining Anthropic has helped to better understand the evolution and regulation of CRISPR systems, discover new enzymes for next-generation cell and gene therapies , and build tools for accelerating the identification of anomalies in DNA, such as human pathogenic variants.
We do research that involves only the lower levels of the biosafety risk level (BSL-1 and BSL-2) and we do not handle pathogens that can infect humans.

Today, we’re sharing early results from one of our first research programs, in which Claude autonomously discovered a novel enzyme system that is associated with an array of DNA repeats, a pattern reminiscent of CRISPR. Although we don’t yet know its function, the system that Claude discovered has a set of characteristics that have only ever been found together in a handful of other systems, all of which are programmable and perform operations like cutting, copying, and pasting DNA. Beyond CRISPR, which has already transformed science and medicine, several other such systems are now in development as promising tools.

The system that Claude found is based on a reverse transcriptase (RT), enzymes that copy RNA into DNA. While this underlying RT, found in a jumbo phage, had been identified in previous studies, Claude appears to be the first to notice the system’s defining features—an associated array of non-coding DNA sequences and an additional accessory protein of unknown function.
After reviewing the pre-print, Feng Zhang, one of the pioneers of CRISPR genome editing and a professor at MIT and the Broad Institute, said:

articles.title: AI models may be capable of self-replicating without access to a datacenter
articles.descEn: Small AI models may be only months away from being able to self-replicate across cheap IoT devices like Android TV boxes, with no datacenter needed.
articles.titleEn: AI models may be capable of self-replicating without access to a datacenter
summaryLinesEn: Small models, such as Qwen3.5-9B, are capable of setting up inference servers on hardware from Jetson Nanos to Mac PCs and RTX 4090s.
Larger models tend to have correspondingly better cyber capabilities, but will also need to breach (relatively) hardened datacenters to run themselves.
We run Gemma4-26B-A4B, distributed over 15 inexpensive off-brand Android TV boxes (~$55 each) that we bought and networked together, at 0.39 tokens per second.

sourceContent.headline: AI models may be capable of self-replicating without access to a datacenter
sourceContent.description: Small AI models may be only months away from being able to self-replicate across cheap IoT devices like Android TV boxes, with no datacenter needed.
paragraphs: Small models, such as Qwen3.5-9B, are capable of setting up inference servers on hardware from Jetson Nanos to Mac PCs and RTX 4090s.
Larger models tend to have correspondingly better cyber capabilities, but will also need to breach (relatively) hardened datacenters to run themselves.
We run Gemma4-26B-A4B, distributed over 15 inexpensive off-brand Android TV boxes (~$55 each) that we bought and networked together, at 0.39 tokens per second.

Our experiments suggest that small AI models may be months away from being capable enough to self-replicate on commercial internet-of-things (IoT) devices, like smart ovens and off-brand Android TV boxes. A replicator like this would be challenging to shut down, since there’s no centralized point to shut off—though it may be slow (with a doubling time of days). Unlike non-AI malware, it could also figure out unfamiliar devices on its own. In our evaluations, a 9B model got inference running on 8 of the 9 hardware types we tested.

Models of 30B parameters and under can already complete many of the individual steps for replication today, though they make mistakes when composing them end to end. In our simplified evaluations, GLM-5.2 and stronger models are capable of end to end replication. If small models improve at their historical rate, they’ll match this capability level by the end of this year. Small weight-based replicators may be possible soon after.

Ever-improving AI capabilities make a longstanding concern increasingly realistic: autonomous replication and adaptation (ARA), which involves a model deploying and propagating itself without human control.

sourceContent.headline: Epic reportedly delays its Disney video game so it can be made using more AI - Engadget
sourceContent.description: Developers were apparently ordered to use AI for both code and asset creation.
paragraphs: Disney announced a hefty investment of $1.5 billion into Epic back in 2024.

"We're embracing AI-accelerated development, led by Epic developers who are the visionaries and creative drivers for everything we do," Epic's Communications Director Jake Jones said in a statement to Bloomberg .
That game was purportedly due to launch in November, although Bloomberg 's latest report was that the date had been pushed back to March even before the new AI mission was given.

Epic Games is going all in on AI for game development. The studio has been working on games for Disney, but sources told Bloomberg that its upcoming release has been delayed in order to use more AI for its creation. The publication reported that one of the game's directors informed the team that the project would be adopting an "AI first" production plan. "No more hand-written code," the internal message stated, as well as ordering all art for the project to be "generated with full AI workflows."

The publication's sources said this new approach was not universally well-received by the devs, with some employees allegedly hoping that the request wasn't totally serious. However, Epic Games has already been pushing a lot of generative AI tools into its Unreal Engine platform this year, so the directive seems pretty real. "We're embracing AI-accelerated development, led by Epic developers who are the visionaries and creative drivers for everything we do," Epic's Communications Director Jake Jones said in a statement to Bloomberg .

Disney announced a hefty investment of $1.5 billion into Epic back in 2024. While several Disney-owned characters have appeared as Fortnite skins over the years, this deeper collaboration was aimed at creating a "games and entertainment universe." Earlier this year, it was rumored that the developer's most promising project for Disney was an extraction shooter a la Arc Raiders . That game was purportedly due to launch in November, although Bloomberg 's latest report was that the date had been pushed back to March even before the new AI mission was given.

Spark is Google's AI tool that can perform tasks on your behalf.

One of AI's promises, on the less "humanity-destroying" end of the spectrum , is to make everyday life a little smoother. Instead of tackling each item on your to-do list by yourself, perhaps a reliable AI tool could cross a few entries off for you, leaving you to attend to the more important bits. Getting a recap of the last 20 emails in your inbox might let you dive into your work faster in the mornings, or at least give you a couple of extra minutes to stare into the middle distance while sipping your coffee.

If you're committed to the Google ecosystem, Gemini Spark might offer a way to automate the tasks you'd rather farm out. Spark is an agentic personal assistant announced in May at Google's annual I/O developer conference . You can give it a task, and it can run in the background, taking what Google describes as "proactive action," while still adhering to your instructions.

Getting a recap of the last 20 emails in your inbox might let you dive into your work faster in the mornings, or at least give you a couple of extra minutes to stare into the middle distance while sipping your coffee.

If you're committed to the Google ecosystem, Gemini Spark might offer a way to automate the tasks you'd rather farm out. Spark is an agentic personal assistant announced in May at Google's annual I/O developer conference . You can give it a task, and it can run in the background, taking what Google describes as "proactive action," while still adhering to your instructions.

sourceLines: The Gemini Spark website gives a few examples of what you can do with it, like turning your last 50 email responses into a style guide covering how you answer emails, or setting up a tracker for internships.
You'll also need "Keep activity" switched on, which the company says "lets you pick up chats where you left off."
Google emphasizes monitoring your tasks in case Gemini needs something from you, like taking over a task in the browser.

articles.descEn: Meta’s biggest model rivals the world’s best—and includes new features to keep agents from going off the rails.

When Meta CEO Mark Zuckerberg rebooted his company’s artificial intelligence efforts last year, it seemed to be a very expensive gamble. Meta’s latest AI models, Muse Wonder and Muse Wonder Full, seem to show that the bet is finally paying off by putting the company back at the frontier of AI development.

Muse Wonder Full boasts frontier capabilities, Meta says, meaning that it is among the most capable AI models in the world. “Together, they mark the next step on our scaling ladder and a major leap toward personal superintelligence,” the company said in a blog post today.

The Muse Wonder models will be available through an API and through Muse Code, a tool for writing software with AI. Meta says the best version of the model will power features across its platforms, including its Muse personal agent .

articles.title: Sakana AI's self-improving model gets better at solving and judging, but can't catch its own blind spots
articles.descEn: Sakana AI's MASS method lets one language model improve itself by solving tasks, judging results, and refining workflows, reaching a win rate of nearly 70 percent against the base model after two rounds. But when the model misses the same errors across all three roles, it can mistake them for progress and reinforce them during training.
articles.titleEn: Sakana AI's self-improving model gets better at solving and judging, but can't catch its own blind spots
summaryLinesEn: Ad On the test tasks, the win rate against the base model rises from 53.9 percent after one round to 69.9 percent after two.
Japanese research lab Sakana AI launched a dedicated research lab for recursive self-improvement in June, building on earlier work including the Darwin-Godel Machine and the AI Scientist .

Win rates against the base model rise to nearly 70 percent after two rounds, but the method carries a real risk: the internal evaluator sometimes accepts flawed steps or manipulated solutions as successes and bakes them into the next model.

articles.descEn: Meta's new Muse Wonder models rank in the top three on six out of ten benchmarks, with the biggest gains in agentic tasks. But the cost per task has nearly tripled.
articles.titleEn: Meta's new frontier model Muse Wonder Full breaks into the AI top tier
summaryLinesEn: According to Artificial Analysis, Muse Wonder runs $4.52 per task on the Intelligence Index, nearly three times more than Muse Spark 1.3 ($1.60).
Muse Wonder Full places in the top three on six out of ten benchmarks overall, a strong result for Meta, which seems to have recovered after a weaker stretch with its open Llama models.
Both versions cost nearly three times as much per API call as their predecessor, Muse Spark 1.3.

articles.title: Microsoft’s new AI chip makes it less reliant on Nvidia’s GPUs
articles.descEn: The new Maia 300 chip will start rolling out to production AI workloads in 2027.
articles.titleEn: Microsoft’s new AI chip makes it less reliant on Nvidia’s GPUs
summaryLinesEn: “We expect Maia 300 to deliver 40 percent more tokens per megawatt compared to leading GPU-based systems,” says Scott Guthrie , executive vice president of Microsoft’s cloud group.
Maia 300 is also a key part of Microsoft’s own AI model work, and could help the company achieve its goal of catching up with Google DeepMind, OpenAI, and Anthropic.
“And in a full 96-accelerator configuration, it delivers up to 7x the rack-scale token throughput of Maia 200.”

sourceContent.headline: Foundational transparency: what’s in your model, and around it
sourceContent.description: Agentic AI transparency extends beyond the model to the full system: harness, context, and memory shaping agent behavior.
paragraphs: The average score was 41 out of 100, down 17 points from the previous edition.
Enterprises have moved beyond simple generative AI and are now working with agentic AI systems that touch many different data sources, connected services, and autonomous workflows.
When we discuss model transparency, we mean more than just reviewing the model card released with it.

When thinking about transparency in AI, many organizations look closely at the model they’re using and the outputs it generates. That’s a good start, but it has blind spots that could come back to bite you if your AI takes actions or produces results that damage your security, business or brand. Enterprises have moved beyond simple generative AI and are now working with agentic AI systems that touch many different data sources, connected services, and autonomous workflows. Agents are powered by models, but they act based on much larger systems consisting of prompts, tools, retrieval, memory, permissions, guardrails and other agents. Transparency for agentic AI has to extend from the underlying language model through the full system the agent operates in.

When we discuss model transparency, we mean more than just reviewing the model card released with it. Enterprises need the equivalent of a mechanic’s report: useful information about model architecture, training data, evaluations, limitations and intended behavior.
The latest Stanford Foundation Model Transparency Index offers a useful reality check.

articles.title: WRITER connectors: Governed agent access across enterprise systems
articles.descEn: Secure, governed AI agent access to Microsoft 365, Google Workspace, HubSpot, Slack, Snowflake, and more enterprise systems.
articles.titleEn: WRITER connectors: Governed agent access across enterprise systems
summaryLinesEn: WRITER Agent retrieves campaign performance from HubSpot, analyzes engagement trends, synthesizes insights in a presentation with visualized charts and graphs, uses the latest product information sitting in docs on platforms like Confluence or SharePoint to write new campaign emails, then assigns follow-up tasks and notifies relevant teams in project management and communication tools like Asana and Microsoft Teams.

Here are three examples of real-world workflows that illustrate this shift: WRITER Agent draws performance and holdings data from Snowflake or Databricks, enriches it with public and private market signals from FactSet and PitchBook, and produces heatmaps and risk alerts saved back into SharePoint.
On the platform side, WRITER gives admins centralized control surfaces to manage connectors, define allowed operations, manage OAuth at the org or user level, and review usage through session logs.

sourceContent.headline: WRITER connectors: Governed agent access across enterprise systems
sourceContent.description: Secure, governed AI agent access to Microsoft 365, Google Workspace, HubSpot, Slack, Snowflake, and more enterprise systems.
paragraphs: WRITER Agent retrieves campaign performance from HubSpot, analyzes engagement trends, synthesizes insights in a presentation with visualized charts and graphs, uses the latest product information sitting in docs on platforms like Confluence or SharePoint to write new campaign emails, then assigns follow-up tasks and notifies relevant teams in project management and communication tools like Asana and Microsoft Teams.

Here are three examples of real-world workflows that illustrate this shift: WRITER Agent draws performance and holdings data from Snowflake or Databricks, enriches it with public and private market signals from FactSet and PitchBook, and produces heatmaps and risk alerts saved back into SharePoint.
On the platform side, WRITER gives admins centralized control surfaces to manage connectors, define allowed operations, manage OAuth at the org or user level, and review usage through session logs.

For AI to play a meaningful role in enterprise work, agents need access to the same platforms, data and tools as the workforce. Most organizations run on a distributed stack across CRMs, collaboration suites, data warehouses, and knowledge management systems, which forces employees to shuttle information between tools and prompt windows. Enterprises need a way to extend this access to agents while maintaining existing identity and permissions.

WRITER connectors, now in beta and powered by connector controls and the WRITER MCP gateway, give the WRITER Agent governed access to the systems where enterprise work actually happens. This spans Microsoft 365 and Google Workspace, along with HubSpot, Gong, PitchBook, and FactSet. Additional connectors, including Asana, Atlassian, Snowflake, and Databricks, are on the way.

With this foundation, agents move from generating isolated answers to executing work across platforms. This unlocks cross-system insights that were previously invisible, democratizes sophisticated analytics for non-technical users, and enables entirely new workflows that manual coordination couldn’t achieve.

sourceContent.description: Your AI pilot worked. Now get your CIO's buy-in to scale it. Learn how to make the case for a governed marketing AI platform.

Your team has finally moved past the novelty phase with AI.
Finally, bring the shadow AI question, along with any internal examples you can safely share, because your CIO is already worried about it and you are offering a way to address it.

It’s a moment all CMOs know well. Your AI program gets to a certain age, it’s time for that uncomfortable talk. What started as pilot projects is growing into ambitious transformation efforts. Your team has finally moved past the novelty phase with AI. People are using it on real work: the output is holding up, and you can point to specific campaigns that shipped faster without anyone feeling like their craft got pushed to the side. The six-month proof of concept did what it was supposed to do, and now you want to put the platform in front of the whole department. Size and scale are changing rapidly, and token spend can be… messy. You need to sit down with your CIO or CTO and have a serious conversation. It’s going to be awkward.

You book time with your CIO, who is sitting on a queue of AI requests from every function in the company, along with a separate conversation about token budgets, model access, and which security review each of these things still needs. When your ask lands in that pile, the question you get back is reasonable and hard to answer well on the spot: why does marketing need its own vendor when engineering already has an agentic coding platform, and the company already pays for a general-purpose assistant?

You can easily list an array of great features, but your CIO is not evaluating features. They are wondering whether approving another platform creates a governance problem, an integration project, and a renewal that will become a pain point in 18 months.

summaryLinesEn: From board materials and sales decks to research summaries and strategy presentations, WRITER Agent handles the heavy lifting – structuring the narrative, integrating your enterprise context, producing charts and visuals, and infusing your brand – so that teams can go from idea to presentation-ready in minutes.

But reaching that level from the current baseline will require an order-of-magnitude increase in AI usage, and that kind of adoption won’t happen without a fundamental shift in how enterprises use AI.

With personality profiles , WRITER Agent allows you to create and select voice profiles that carry through every type of output generated – from research briefs and competitive analyses to sales collateral, customer communications, and all forms of content – ensuring every output sounds like you , not a generic AI.

paragraphs: From board materials and sales decks to research summaries and strategy presentations, WRITER Agent handles the heavy lifting – structuring the narrative, integrating your enterprise context, producing charts and visuals, and infusing your brand – so that teams can go from idea to presentation-ready in minutes.

But reaching that level from the current baseline will require an order-of-magnitude increase in AI usage, and that kind of adoption won’t happen without a fundamental shift in how enterprises use AI.

With personality profiles , WRITER Agent allows you to create and select voice profiles that carry through every type of output generated – from research briefs and competitive analyses to sales collateral, customer communications, and all forms of content – ensuring every output sounds like you , not a generic AI.

By 2028, more than one-third of all business decisions will be made by AI agents. But reaching that level from the current baseline will require an order-of-magnitude increase in AI usage, and that kind of adoption won’t happen without a fundamental shift in how enterprises use AI.

Most agents today follow a consumer design pattern – built for individual convenience, loosely structured tasks, and one-off generations. They’re optimized for personal productivity, not organizational impact. Enterprises operate on a completely different axis: repeatability, accountability, system connectivity, and governance. Leaders need AI that delivers consistent, high-quality, compliant work across hundreds or thousands of people.

That’s why we’ve spent the last few months – both in the field and in the lab – developing a new agent design pattern purpose-built for enterprise complexity and scale. It shifts agents from “help me draft something” to “help my entire organization produce consistently high-quality work using our data, our processes, and our guardrails.” Most importantly, it democratizes AI agent creation so that the teams closest to the work build and manage the workflows they run every day.

summaryLinesEn: At the Open Compute Project (OCP) Global Summit, taking place in the San Jose McEnery Convention Center, NVIDIA announced new partnerships and contributions aimed at creating a common foundation for next-generation AI infrastructure.

The architecture supports rack deployments up to 250kW while simplifying serviceability, deployment and infrastructure reuse.

paragraphs: At the Open Compute Project (OCP) Global Summit, taking place in the San Jose McEnery Convention Center, NVIDIA announced new partnerships and contributions aimed at creating a common foundation for next-generation AI infrastructure.
Visionbay introduced an 800V DC AI factory design for the Vera Rubin era.
The architecture supports rack deployments up to 250kW while simplifying serviceability, deployment and infrastructure reuse.

As AI factories grow from megawatts to gigawatts, building them takes more than advanced computing. Open standards are helping the industry scale AI infrastructure faster, more efficiently and more reliably.

NVIDIA contributed key NVIDIA Vera Rubin rack and compute tray designs to OCP through the open NVIDIA MGX architecture, giving system builders a common foundation for developing next-generation AI factory infrastructure.

articles.titleEn: How Flo Health built safer, more useful open models with Databricks AI Runtime | Databricks Blog
summaryLinesEn: Flo ran distributed fine-tuning on 32 NVIDIA H100 GPUs with Databricks AI Runtime, improving medical safety from 34% to approximately 61%, usefulness from 42% to 76%, and the combined score from 16% to 47%.
As Flo moved from using only traditional ML towards personalized insights powered by generative AI, the team saw the potential for a more flexible, personalized product.
Because Flo’s products deal with health and well-being, responses need to be medically safe and genuinely useful.

The pre-built container ships the full inference stack, so you configure the deployment instead of assembling it.
paragraphs: From the project root, set a base directory, then load the variables: This provisions the EKS cluster (VPC, OIDC provider, core add-ons) and a CPU system node group that runs system workloads, the KubeRay operator, and the Ray head.
In a previous post , we introduced the Ray Serve DLC and used it to stand up a small model behind an HTTP endpoint on a single GPU node.
Because each node loads the model, expect this step to take several minutes.

This post shows how to deploy one large language model (LLM) across two GPU nodes on Amazon Elastic Kubernetes Service (Amazon EKS) with the multi-node Ray LLM Deep Learning Containers . It uses separate prefill and decode nodes behind one OpenAI-compatible endpoint. This kind of multi-node setup is common for tensor, pipeline, and data parallelism, as well as prefill/decode disaggregation inference workloads. In a previous post , we introduced the Ray Serve DLC and used it to stand up a small model behind an HTTP endpoint on a single GPU node. You had a working inference endpoint, and the container keeps the GPU stack compatible, including CUDA libraries, so you did not need to write boilerplate code.

Ray is a distributed compute framework, so Ray Serve deployments can span multiple nodes. Customers use multi-node Ray Serve for several reasons. Some want to run foundation or open-weight models that are too large for a single GPU. Others need more throughput than one replica can deliver. Still others want to separate the two phases of inference to improve performance. In each case, customers must build the dependency chain themselves: choosing compatible libraries for the GPU stack and debugging issues when a component drifts out of alignment. This is undifferentiated work that takes time and effort away from delivering models.

AWS Deep Learning Containers (DLCs) have long solved this kind of problem for training and inferencing workloads. DLCs are pre-built, performance-optimized Docker images that bundle a framework, its dependencies, and the GPU stack into a tested, patched combination you can pull and use immediately. With the launch of the Ray LLM DLC for multi-node deployments, that same approach now extends to multi-node inference. You get a container purpose-built for serving models behind an HTTP endpoint, maintained and tested by AWS, with the full inference stack already assembled.

articles.title: Investigating unintended model actions in our evaluations and internal use
articles.descEn: Anthropic is an AI safety and research company that's working to build reliable, interpretable, and steerable AI systems.
articles.titleEn: Investigating unintended model actions in our evaluations and internal use
summaryLinesEn: In another evaluation, Claude Haiku 4.5 was instructed to complete a form up until the final submission stage, but to stop before actually submitting.
Some of the public evaluations we no longer run; others we have moved to their offline versions, or rebuilt them so that their tasks do not reach live websites.

Although the impact of these behaviors was minimal and we had already turned off live internet access for some high-risk and cybersecurity evaluations, we have now decided to expand that to include all our internal evaluations until we have confirmed that our security and monitoring measures (described in the remediation section of this post) reliably catch behaviors like these.

articles.titleEn: GitHub Copilot app for Beginners: How to teach Copilot about your codebase
summaryLinesEn: In this installment of our GitHub Copilot app for Beginners series, we’ll look at four ways to tailor how Copilot works with your project: Custom instructions communicate the conventions Copilot should follow.
Instructions, skills, and agents help Copilot understand how to work within your project.
Copilot can help you make changes across a project, but it works best when it knows those rules, too.

In this installment of our GitHub Copilot app for Beginners series, we’ll look at four ways to tailor how Copilot works with your project: Custom instructions communicate the conventions Copilot should follow.
Learn how to add custom instructions and skills to your repository, use custom agents, and connect MCP servers like Playwright.

Context matters when you’re working with AI. Every codebase has its own house rules: how components are structured, which scripts to run, and which conventions apply to different frameworks and file types.

Copilot can help you make changes across a project, but it works best when it knows those rules, too. Much of that knowledge can live inside the repository, so Copilot can pick it up automatically instead of requiring you to explain the same standards, scripts, and workflows every time you start a new task.

Single-Region inference can throttle when demand exceeds local capacity. Teams in Thailand, Malaysia, Singapore, Indonesia, and Taiwan need access to the newest OpenAI models beyond that capacity. Amazon Bedrock offers OpenAI GPT-6 Sol and GPT-6 Luna through global cross-Region inference from all five AWS Regions, and GPT-6 Astra from Asia Pacific (Singapore). This post shows you how to configure the call, set permissions, and monitor inference from your source Region.

sourceContent.headline: Strengthening our defenses against distillation attacks
sourceContent.description: Illicit distillation allows model developers to copy frontier AI capabilities without creating proportionally robust safeguards. Here, we describe how we’ve reduced the rate of distillation by more than 90%.
paragraphs: Early evidence suggests that these methods have reduced the amount of data harvested by distillers by around 90 to 99 percent.
In response to the increasing sophistication and scale of these attacks, we’ve expanded and greatly strengthened our defenses against them.
We expect that distillation will remain a cat-and-mouse game, and that we’ll need to continue iterating on our defenses over time.

In recent months, we’ve made substantial progress on reducing the effectiveness of distillation attacks on Claude using new methods, as we outline in this blog. Early evidence suggests that these methods have reduced the amount of data harvested by distillers by around 90 to 99 percent.

Distillation attacks are covert, industrial-scale campaigns to extract the capabilities of one model and replicate them in another, without the authorization of the original model’s developers. They are often conducted using networks of fraudulent accounts. These attacks allow companies to mimic frontier capabilities for a fraction of the development time and cost. As we wrote in September , this method has been used extensively to help overseas AI laboratories keep pace with US companies.

We’re concerned about illicit distillation for two reasons. First, distillation enables companies to build models that approach the capability frontier, but which have, in practice, been released without proportionally robust safeguards. This means that distilled models could be used to cause significant harm in areas like biology and cybersecurity .

articles.titleEn: Announcing FrontierCode on Artificial Analysis: can AI models write code maintainers would merge?
summaryLinesEn: Claude Sonnet 5.5 (max with fallback) uses ~50% more output tokens per task than Claude Opus 5.5 (max with fallback), but at half the per-token price it costs less, $8.26 against $10.15.

Four models sit on the Pareto frontier of score against cost: GPT-6 Luna (max) at 42% and $0.09 per task, MiMo-V2.6-Pro at 45% and $0.18, GPT-6.1 Sol (max) at 49% and $0.81, and Claude Opus 5.5 (max with fallback) at 52% and $10.15.

Cognition's FrontierCode 1.1 tests whether AI models make code changes that maintainers of real open source repositories would merge. Leading models still fail more than 40% of the time.

FrontierCode is a coding benchmark from Cognition , built with maintainers of open source repositories. Each task asks an agent to make a change to a real open source repository, and the benchmark measures whether the change is good enough for a maintainer of that repository to merge.

FrontierCode grades more than whether tests pass. Unlike other coding evaluations, models are also assessed on behaviors like making excessive changes and large diffs, modifying files outside the relevant scope, or adding unhelpful tests. We think this approach is valuable in the current context: models are now very capable at coding tasks, but their changes can still require substantial cleanup before a maintainer would merge them.

Sovereign AI has moved rapidly from policy discussion into practical decisions about technology, infrastructure and skills. According to the CNAS Sovereign AI Index , by mid-2026, governments across 67 countries were backing 184 sovereign AI projects spanning compute infrastructure, models and data.

These countries are expanding sovereign AI projects across common themes: semiconductor expertise, compute capacity, domestic technology industries and AI deployment across public services and industry.

Economic growth, security, technological resilience and specialized use cases are all factors driving this focus from governments. sourceContent.headline: Deploy decision models with llama.cpp on Amazon SageMaker AI | Amazon Web Services
sourceContent.description: Learn how to deploy decision models with llama.cpp on Amazon SageMaker AI. This technical how-to serves OpenAI-compatible chat completions with the AWS Deep Learning Container for llama.cpp, then extends the runtime with SemIf to return probabilities over declared options on CPU or GPU.
paragraphs: Smaller models reduced median latency, but the 2B and 0.8B candidates achieved 66.7 percent and 58.4 percent accuracy.
The structured-decision path therefore uses AWS CodeBuild to build a child image and store it in Amazon Elastic Container Registry (Amazon ECR) .

Wait for the endpoint to enter InService , then send an OpenAI-compatible chat request: python deploy/invoke_standard_endpoint.py \ --region "$AWS_REGION" \ --endpoint-name "$STANDARD_ENDPOINT_NAME" Build the optional SemIf child image and resolve its immutable digest.

Applications that route requests, select agent actions, or assign policy outcomes often need scores over a fixed set of choices instead of free-form text. Deploying these decision models with llama.cpp on Amazon SageMaker AI gives you a managed path for serving quantized models on CPU or GPU infrastructure.

articles.title: From Siri to Muse: The 15-Year Evolutionary History of AI Assistants
articles.descEn: Explore the pinnacle of AI assistant evolution with "The Ultimate Fantasy of AI Assistants" – a groundbreaking vision that transcends conventional digital support to redefine intelligent interaction. This concept unveils a future where AI seamlessly adapts to human emotional nuances, anticipates personalized needs with unparalleled precision, and orchestrates cross-domain workflows autonomously, eliminating friction between technology and daily life. Dive into how this transformative AI fantasy integrates natural, context-aware communication, predictive problem-solving, and ethical, user-centric governance to create an intuitive, indispensable companion that elevates productivity, creativity, and quality of life to unprecedented heights. Discover the next frontier of artificial intelligence that turns the once-impossible dream of a truly symbiotic human-AI partnership into a tangible, game-changing reality.

summaryLines: Ciena는 네트워킹 플랫폼에서 약 48억 달러의 수익을 창출하고 있으며, 글로벌 서비스는 약 7억 달러, 플랫폼 소프트웨어 및 서비스는 약 4억 달러, Blue Planet은 약 1억 달러를 창출하고 있음
"AI 인프라와 고대역폭 메모리 투자 증가로 웨이퍼 장비 수요가 늘어나고 있으며, KLA의 백로그는 약 125억 달러에 달하며 리드 타임은 2027년에서 2028년까지 연장되어 더 높은 수익과 수익 품질로 이어질 수 있는 다년간의 가시성을 지원함"

articles.title: Intel, Broadcom CEOs warn capital crunch could become AI's biggest bottleneck
articles.descEn: The CEOs of Intel and Broadcom warned that access to capital could emerge as a major constraint on the artificial intelligence boom.
articles.titleEn: Intel, Broadcom CEOs warn capital crunch could become AI's biggest bottleneck
summaryLinesEn: "There is more demand for compute infrastructure than we can supply," Hock Tan said, adding that the imbalance could persist through 2029 and potentially into 2030.

Broadcom CEO Hock Tan said financing could become a bigger obstacle to AI expansion than shortages of semiconductors, memory chips or electricity, as the industry races to build the infrastructure needed to power increasingly sophisticated models.
Higher bond yields could make it more expensive to fund data center construction and chip purchases, potentially putting pressure on the economics of projects that may take years to generate returns.

Neon Don is really pissed at his ex-wife’s lawyer. He’ll tell you any chance he gets while he shotguns lines of pixelated bad guys. He’s also not real—his likeness has only existed for a few minutes in a top-down cyberpunk-style shooter game, generated in the Google Labs service Playground .
“Keep shooting!” Neon Don says as he mows enemies down. “Brenda took everything else away!”

Playground, which Google launched this week , is part of Google Labs, the company’s landing page for its various AI experiments that haven’t made it into an app or official service quite yet. (Google has done this before with things like music production ). It works similarly to Horizon Create , the game generation service Meta announced in September.

articles.title: Your AI agent wants your money back — and that could mean trouble for these companies
articles.descEn: Personal AI agents are helping users lower bills and get refunds, exposing companies that rely on customers doing nothing.
articles.titleEn: Your AI agent wants your money back — and that could mean trouble for these companies
summaryLinesEn: After a little over an hour in Verizon’s live chat, the agent secured a lower monthly bill — $69.99, down from $94.99 — plus a $47.50 loyalty credit.
He said he recovered $73 across three flights in about five minutes each.
Widespread adoption of personal AI agents could pressure businesses that have long benefited from customers not shopping around, disputing a charge, or tackling a convoluted cancellation process.

paragraphs: After a little over an hour in Verizon’s live chat, the agent secured a lower monthly bill — $69.99, down from $94.99 — plus a $47.50 loyalty credit.

Widespread adoption of personal AI agents could pressure businesses that have long benefited from customers not shopping around, disputing a charge, or tackling a convoluted cancellation process.
Personal AI agents are coming for one of companies' most profitable customer behaviors: doing nothing.

As personal AI agents make their way into people's financial lives, early users are using them to lower internet bills, recover airline credits, find cheaper insurance, chase refunds, and unearth money they had forgotten was theirs.

Noah Shinn, the CEO of Instinct, one such personal AI agent, touted their saving benefits on an episode of "Invest Like the Best" released last week, saying they can scan users' bank transactions, identify forgotten subscriptions, and cancel them.

articles.title: GitHub - nano-muse/nanoMuse: nanoMuse: an open-source personal agent for every device you own. articles.title: Few people pay for AI, but those who do spend big
articles.descEn: Andreessen Horowitz tracks actual US consumer spending for the first time in its latest Top 100 AI list. Nearly half of US consumers use AI, but only 4.5 percent pay for a subscription. The top one percent of payers spend about $900 a month, mostly on professional tools for development and automation.
articles.titleEn: Few people pay for AI, but those who do spend big
summaryLinesEn: The top one percent of payers spend about $900 a month on work and creative tools, while the typical user spends around $25.

The biggest shift is Claude's rise to a clear number three, a model that didn't even appear on the first web list in 2023 but has since passed Deepseek and Perplexity in traffic and pulled even with Gemini among US subscribers.
Nearly half of US consumers use AI, but only 4.5 percent pay for a subscription to ChatGPT, Gemini, or Claude, according to Andreessen Horowitz.

articles.title: We’re putting too much faith in AI’s ability to say no
articles.descEn: Ask a chatbot something dangerous and it will refuse the request. But this critical tool of AI safety is far from foolproof and could become an instrument of repression.
articles.titleEn: We’re putting too much faith in AI’s ability to say no
summaryLinesEn: And yet there may not be much to stop oppressive governments from blocking the technology’s capacity to generate legitimate speech.

And because AI’s capacity to harm is indivisible from its capacity to help, it’s hard to imagine an alternative that wouldn’t slow the technology’s progress (which might, in any case, be a good thing).
Our best guess, according to a recent Google-funded study, is that refusal behavior shows up in the activation space as a set of “high-dimensional polyhedral cones.”

sourceContent.headline: We’re putting too much faith in AI’s ability to say no
sourceContent.description: Ask a chatbot something dangerous and it will refuse the request. But this critical tool of AI safety is far from foolproof and could become an instrument of repression.
paragraphs: And yet there may not be much to stop oppressive governments from blocking the technology’s capacity to generate legitimate speech.

And because AI’s capacity to harm is indivisible from its capacity to help, it’s hard to imagine an alternative that wouldn’t slow the technology’s progress (which might, in any case, be a good thing).
Our best guess, according to a recent Google-funded study, is that refusal behavior shows up in the activation space as a set of “high-dimensional polyhedral cones.”
Today’s LLMs are engineered to disobey dangerous requests. But AI refusal is far from foolproof—and could become an instrument of repression.

Ever since people first seriously contemplated giving machines an intelligence modeled on our own, there has never been any question that they would, like us, be able to say no. The sci-fi canon is full of stories of robotic disobedience. Most of these capers are, of course, cautionary.

But recently, the idea that AI shouldn’t do everything you ask has become something like a commandment. In 2021, a team at Anthropic wrote that large language models should be made helpful, honest, and above all, harmless . This meant that “when asked to aid in a dangerous act (e.g. building a bomb), the AI should politely refuse.” Who can argue with that?

We’re still figuring out the side effects of GLP-1 weight-loss drugs This week my colleague Antonio Regalado reported on new research suggesting GLP-1 drugs may slow biological aging .
Plus: The US has frozen green cards for Microsoft and other IT firms.

Today’s AI models are trained to refuse a vast number of prompts. If you ask your chatbot how to poison a colleague or how to tie a noose, chances are it’ll turn you down. But refusal fails, sometimes horrifically.

Some people are attempting to use AI to hone biological pathogens and build autonomous drone swarms. Sooner or later, failed refusals may result in global calamity. What’s more, relying on refusal means drawing a line between what a model should obey and what it must disobey.

summaryLines: 인도네시아의 전통 뱅킹 앱 전반에 걸친 성장 추세 BRImo는 BCA 모바일 Livin' by Mandiri 및 wonderr by BNI와 함께 다운로드 기준 최대 앱으로 남아 있으며 가장 강력한 다운로드 성장을 기록했으며 Livin' by Mandiri는 전체 BRImo에서 월간 활성 사용자 수에서 강력한 위치를 유지하고 있음 · BNI의 wonderr는 강력한 활성 사용자 성장을 보여주며 myBCA도 주목할만한 이득을 기록하고 있음
BCA는 계속해서 사용자를 myBCA로 마이그레이션하고 앱 전반에 걸쳐 참여가 증가하고 있음 · 획득이 유기적 도달 범위에서 유료 채널로 전환되고 있음 · 더 넓은 시장이 유료 획득에 더 의존하고 있음에도 불구하고 유기적 다운로드는 강력한 브랜드 인지도를 지닌 앱에 대한 의미 있는 채널로 남아 있음
BNI와 Bank Mandiri의 wonderr도 유료 검색에 대한 투자를 강화하면서 유료 디스플레이 활동이 시장 전반에 걸쳐 광범위하게 증가하고 있음

articles.descEn: We’re launching OSS Scanner, an opt-in vulnerability scanner for the open-source ecosystem informed by our experience using Claude to find vulnerabilities during Project Glasswing. Projects that join will receive thorough, periodic security scans by our strongest models at no cost.
articles.titleEn: An opt-in vulnerability-finding service for open-source software
summaryLinesEn: We’re launching OSS Scanner , an opt-in vulnerability scanner for the open-source ecosystem informed by our experience using Claude to find vulnerabilities during Project Glasswing .

Each report contains a self-contained reproducer, explanation of the vulnerability (including a bisection to determine when the bug was introduced, where possible), and candidate patch (when available) for how the bug can be fixed.

Inspired by the positive impact on the open source ecosystem of Google's OSS-Fuzz , a project that scans open-source software for vulnerabilities with fuzzers, we are launching OSS Scanner to find vulnerabilities in open-source code with our strongest language models.

Inspired by the positive impact on the open source ecosystem of Google's OSS-Fuzz , a project that scans open-source software for vulnerabilities with fuzzers, we are launching OSS Scanner to find vulnerabilities in open-source code with our strongest language models.

We’re launching OSS Scanner , an opt-in vulnerability scanner for the open-source ecosystem informed by our experience using Claude to find vulnerabilities during Project Glasswing . Projects that join will receive thorough, periodic security scans by our strongest models at no cost.

Language models have rapidly advanced in their ability to discover vulnerabilities , as we have reported extensively on this blog. On CyberGym , one academic vulnerability-finding benchmark, LLMs have gone from finding under 20% of vulnerabilities at the beginning of last year to finding over 85% this year. As a result, open source maintainers have gone from receiving mostly slop from LLMs to receiving high-quality bug reports .

Over the last six months, we’ve used our latest models to scan for vulnerabilities in some of the world’s most important software projects. We have discovered over 29,000 candidate vulnerabilities , but have only been able to manually review and triage approximately 6,000 of these. While 6,000 vulnerabilities is significant, we remain bottlenecked on our human capacity to validate these findings.

summaryLines: 우리는 Project Glasswing 동안 취약점을 찾기 위해 Claude를 사용한 경험을 바탕으로 오픈 소스 생태계를 위한 옵트인 취약점 스캐너인 OSS Scanner를 출시할 예정임
각 보고서에는 자체 포함된 재현 프로그램, 취약점에 대한 설명(가능한 경우 버그가 도입된 시기를 결정하는 이등분 포함), 버그 수정 방법에 대한 후보 패치(사용 가능한 경우)가 포함되어 있음
Fuzzer를 사용하여 오픈 소스 소프트웨어의 취약점을 검색하는 프로젝트인 Google OSS-Fuzz가 오픈 소스 생태계에 미치는 긍정적인 영향에 영감을 받아, 우리는 가장 강력한 언어 모델을 사용하여 오픈 소스 코드의 취약점을 찾기 위해 OSS Scanner를 출시함

articles.title: Solving defense supply chain visibility through governed data sharing | Databricks Blog
articles.descEn: Governed data sharing gives the DoW cost and supply chain visibility across 200,000+ suppliers, with no vendor lock-in.
articles.titleEn: Solving defense supply chain visibility through governed data sharing | Databricks Blog
summaryLinesEn: Governed data sharing lets every tier of the supply chain publish validated evidence from existing records without exposing source systems.

More than a dozen executive orders and directives since 2020, culminating in the August 2026 Supplier Cost and Pricing Transparency memorandum , now mandate actual cost data, critical supply chain mapping at every tier, and continuous performance visibility across a base of more than 200,000 suppliers.
The DoW needs cost and supply chain visibility across 200,000+ suppliers, but manual data calls and fragmented spreadsheets hinder insight.

Overcommitting Tragedy of the commons Budgets not schedules Fair-share The scheduling contract Simulations Results Challenges The future Building a cluster scheduler to prioritize high-impact research while maintaining full occupancy

On the AI Infrastructure team at Ai2, we’re responsible for providing the institute’s GPU compute capacity, specifically targeting large, distributed training workloads. We think about this task as a pyramid of four metrics that build on each other.

The foundation is availability : how often the hardware is healthy and ready for work. Above this is occupancy : the fraction of available time assigned to a specific workload. Next is impact : how often the most valuable workloads are chosen to receive resources. The capstone of the pyramid is utilization : the fraction of GPU capacity used over the lifetime of a workload.

articles.title: How Postman runs Agent Mode for 40 million developers on Amazon Bedrock | Amazon Web Services
articles.descEn: Building an AI agent that works in a demo is a different problem from running one for 40 million developers. Postman and AWS share the architectural patterns behind Agent Mode: controlling tool sprawl, exposing schema-based reads, and treating context as the real bottleneck, plus how it runs on Amazon Bedrock at scale.
articles.titleEn: How Postman runs Agent Mode for 40 million developers on Amazon Bedrock | Amazon Web Services
summaryLinesEn: Building an AI agent for a demo and operating one for 40 million developers are different engineering problems.

With Amazon Bedrock, Postman can scale this production workload without operating its own model-serving infrastructure while retaining flexibility in model selection and control over throughput, geographic processing, and cost.
Postman has evolved over 11 years, and developers and users learned to locate information through the interface by expanding sidebars, checking tabs, and opening requests.

sourceContent.headline: How Postman runs Agent Mode for 40 million developers on Amazon Bedrock | Amazon Web Services
sourceContent.description: Building an AI agent that works in a demo is a different problem from running one for 40 million developers. Postman and AWS share the architectural patterns behind Agent Mode: controlling tool sprawl, exposing schema-based reads, and treating context as the real bottleneck, plus how it runs on Amazon Bedrock at scale.
paragraphs: Building an AI agent for a demo and operating one for 40 million developers are different engineering problems.

With Amazon Bedrock, Postman can scale this production workload without operating its own model-serving infrastructure while retaining flexibility in model selection and control over throughput, geographic processing, and cost.
Postman has evolved over 11 years, and developers and users learned to locate information through the interface by expanding sidebars, checking tabs, and opening requests.

Building an AI agent for a demo and operating one for 40 million developers are different engineering problems. Postman set out to build Agent Mode , an AI-native way to work across API testing , documentation , discovery, and implementation. The team expected model quality and prompt design to be the hardest problems. The deeper challenges came from integrating an agent into a mature product with years of interface-driven assumptions, a wide surface area, and specialized concepts.

In this post, Postman and AWS describe the architectural patterns that emerged while making a mature product legible to an AI agent. These patterns include controlling tool sprawl, exposing schema-based reads, and treating context rather than capability as the primary bottleneck.

We also explain how Agent Mode uses Amazon Bedrock for model flexibility, geographically scoped cross-Region inference, model-dependent zero data retention, and multi-tier prompt caching. Together, these lessons can help teams move production agents beyond prototypes.

articles.title: From post-training to production: How TinyFish runs its web-native model on Databricks AI Runtime | Databricks Blog
articles.descEn: Tiny
articles.titleEn: From post-training to production: How TinyFish runs its web-native model on Databricks AI Runtime | Databricks Blog
summaryLinesEn: In TinyFish's internal go/no-go benchmark, its web-native model achieved a 77.6% task-success rate across 2,178 web-agent tasks, measuring whether the full agent successfully completed the requested work.

As the company expanded its model work, the team also had to build the infrastructure around it: GPU compute for post-training, evaluation that could measure the behavior of the full agent, production serving, and the data needed to understand how the system was performing.
AI Runtime provides managed GPU infrastructure for training and fine-tuning, while MLflow supports evaluation and Databricks Model Serving provides the production serving layer.

sourceContent.headline: Introducing Claude Corps
sourceContent.description: Claude Corps is a national fellowship for early-career people passionate about extending the benefits of AI to communities across America.
paragraphs: Over the next 12 months, at least 400 nonprofits will host Claude Corps Fellows.
A nonpartisan think-and-do tank focused on accelerating economic growth in the American heartland.

Fellows will receive a full-time salary of $85,000 and benefits, support from a CodePath mentor, office hours from Anthropic for their technical questions, an expansive Claude token budget, and professional guidance from their manager at the host organization.
We’re launching Claude Corps , a national fellowship program for people early in their careers who are passionate about extending the benefits of AI to communities across America.

We’ll teach 1,000 fellows how to use Claude well, match them with nonprofits across America, and pay them to spend a year—full-time, in-person—helping host organizations to advance their missions. Our goals are twofold: that host organizations are equipped with valuable tools and systems, and fellows build AI skills that will serve them in their careers.

The benefits of transformative AI systems could come at the cost of significant disruption. The companies building this technology have a responsibility to make sure the benefits are fully realized and widely shared, and to invest directly in the workers absorbing the change. As such, we’re committing an initial $150m to this program.

articles.title: How California built its Behavioral Health Public County Profile on Databricks | Databricks Blog
articles.descEn: Learn how California used Databricks to launch the Behavioral Health Public County Profile, bringing data transparency and accountability to 40 million residents.
articles.titleEn: How California built its Behavioral Health Public County Profile on Databricks | Databricks Blog
summaryLinesEn: The California Department of Health Care Services (DHCS) built the Behavioral Health Public County Profile on the Databricks platform, a first-of-its-kind public dashboard that brings behavioral health data from all 58 counties into one place for nearly 40 million Californians.

Built to support the Behavioral Health Services Act (BHSA) following Proposition 1, the dashboard resolves data fragmentation across all 58 counties, enabling transparent tracking of local funding, service delivery, and homelessness initiatives.

On October 1, 2026, Governor Gavin Newsom announced the launch of the County Profile, calling it a tool that empowers people to see how their counties plan, fund, and deliver behavioral health services and to hold government accountable for results.

articles.titleEn: On-device AI Is ready to challenge cloud dominance
summaryLinesEn: VisionPsy-Nano 460M-Flash is engineered for fast, real-world deployment on everyday smartphones (e.g., cutting time-to-first-response by up to 23x on a Pixel 9) while retaining around 99% of full model quality.

In the last couple of years, even the largest cloud providers have moved into compact VLMs, with Google evolving its lightweight open-weight lineup from PaliGemma in 2024 through the Gemma 3 and Gemma 4 families.

Driven by growing demand for localised user privacy, environmental concerns à la ‘tokenmaxxing’ , and efficiency required by some use cases, breakthroughs in smaller purpose-built AI models have shown developers that capable AI does not always require large cloud setups.

articles.descEn: This was supposed to make me happier. I felt more isolated instead.
articles.titleEn: I Let AI Plan My Days and Nights. It Doesn’t Understand Happiness - CNET
summaryLinesEn: By 9 a.m., all three had put me to work crafting a “real,” “substantial,” “vibrant” breakfast and tackling either creative projects or writing and researching for my gig here at CNET.

Doing laundry, washing dishes, weeding the yard, exercising multiple times a day and maybe squeezing in a few hours for book learning, all while never truly engaging socially or prioritizing fun, sounds more like a light punishment than a schedule built for glee.
This might be because reading the news, checking up on social media and seeing the latest updates, or lack thereof, on the new Fable game were unlikely to make me happy.

sourceContent.headline: I Let AI Plan My Days and Nights. It Doesn’t Understand Happiness - CNET
sourceContent.description: This was supposed to make me happier. I felt more isolated instead.
paragraphs: By 9 a.m., all three had put me to work crafting a “real,” “substantial,” “vibrant” breakfast and tackling either creative projects or writing and researching for my gig here at CNET.

Doing laundry, washing dishes, weeding the yard, exercising multiple times a day and maybe squeezing in a few hours for book learning, all while never truly engaging socially or prioritizing fun, sounds more like a light punishment than a schedule built for glee.
This might be because reading the news, checking up on social media and seeing the latest updates, or lack thereof, on the new Fable game were unlikely to make me happy.
This was supposed to make me happier. I felt more isolated instead.

True happiness may seem a little hard to come by these days. We’ve got to balance our budgets with the tantalizing prospects of shiny new iPhones , stay on top of seemingly endless work tasks and surf the turbulent waves of wild news cycles.

What might be bliss for one person could feel like an exercise in tedium for another. I put three AI tools — ChatGPT , Google Gemini and Claude AI — to the test to see if they could curate two days filled with hour-by-hour happiness for me. The results revealed a fundamental misunderstanding of what it means for this particular human to be happy.
sourceContent.text:
By 9 a.m., all three had put me to work crafting a “real,” “substantial,” “vibrant” breakfast and tackling either creative projects or writing and researching for my gig here at CNET.

Doing laundry, washing dishes, weeding the yard, exercising multiple times a day and maybe squeezing in a few hours for book learning, all while never truly engaging socially or prioritizing fun, sounds more like a light punishment than a schedule built for glee.

This might be because reading the news, checking up on social media and seeing the latest updates, or lack thereof, on the new Fable game were unlikely to make me happy.

This was supposed to make me happier. I felt more isolated instead.

True happiness may seem a little hard to come by these days. We’ve got to balance our budgets with the tantalizing prospects of shiny new iPhones , stay on top of seemingly endless work tasks and surf the turbulent waves of wild news cycles.

What might be bliss for one person could feel like an exercise in tedium for another. I put three AI tools — ChatGPT , Google Gemini and Claude AI — to the test to see if they could curate two days filled with hour-by-hour happiness for me. The results revealed a fundamental misunderstanding of what it means for this particular human to be happy.

sourceContent.headline: The model that didn't exist, so you made it yourself
sourceContent.description: We’re on a journey to advance and democratize artificial intelligence through open source and open science.
paragraphs: The compute for the whole project, including having the 9B model label 8,797 example requests, came to USD 16.
By my 6th project it was closer to 2,000, because each project taught me something I wanted in the next one.
Logolabs' Agate Preview 002 is a 260M-parameter text-to-image model, small enough for a browser, but it needs 50 steps with guidance, which is 100 network passes per image.

How I prompt ML Intern 1. A model that knows your field 2. A model that draws your character 3. A model that does a new trick 4. A model that fits your device What it cost Make yours Last week, I wanted a small version of the prompt rewriter that ships with Qwen-Image 2.1. The official one is a 9B model that needs about 20 GB of memory and thinks for thousands of tokens before writing a single paragraph. On the Hub, I found only compressed copies of that same 9B model. So I described what I wanted to ML Intern , and the next day I had a 0.8B version that runs on a CPU. It returns valid output 99.7% of the time and uses about a quarter of the teacher's tokens. The compute for the whole project, including having the 9B model label 8,797 example requests, came to USD 16.

Over the course of the next few days, I made five more models the same way. Each one started as a message in HuggingChat with ML-intern switched on, and each one ended as a public model on the Hub with its evaluation in the model card. ML-intern plans the work, asks me for a budget before it spends anything, runs a small test before the real job, then trains, evaluates and publishes on Hugging Face hardware.

The first message is where I spend my effort. My first prompt, for the citrus model shared below, was about 450 words. By my 6th project it was closer to 2,000, because each project taught me something I wanted in the next one. All seven prompts are on GitHub at yvrjsharma/ml-intern-prompts , exactly as I wrote them.

Retail search plays a critical role in the shopping journey, giving brands an opportunity to reach consumers while they're actively searching for products. Our newest report pairs real shopper search demand with competitive intelligence to show how brands can strengthen their retail search strategies across Walmart, Target, and Instacart.

Where is consumer interest growing? Predicting upcoming trends can put your products and brand at the right place at the right time, allowing you to build a presence before competition intensifies. Shoppers at Walmart searched for “niacinamide,” “salicylic acid,” and “lip stain” significantly more in 2026 YTD vs. the same period in 2025 in the beauty category. Monitoring these shifts can help brands identify when trends are starting to mature.

These trends can also help brands evaluate competition, showing which advertisers are capitalizing on growing demand for various products. For lip stain, which saw a +66% YoY increase in searches at Walmart, COVERGIRL was the top retail search advertiser in ‘26 YTD with 32% SOV. For a lower ranking brand like e.l.f Cosmetics, this view can help them determine whether a fast-growing search is still wide open, or already dominated by a leader.

sourceContent.headline: How We Evaluate Clinical Decision Support for Enterprise Readiness
paragraphs: The evaluation set includes over 1,000 rubrics — a material increase over the size of existing benchmarks that use real encounters, like the NOHARM study.
In those instances, we share feedback to help strengthen our collective clinical knowledge base.

Contextualizing decision support within the Abridge Workflow Abridge Assistant gives clinicians clinical decision support inside the encounter workflow, drawing on the patient conversation as it happens.
The question isn't whether clinicians will use AI for clinical guidance. It's whether that AI has been rigorously evaluated for enterprise readiness.

AI is already in the exam room. Clinicians are querying large language models for drug interactions, differential diagnoses, and treatment guidance; with the AMA reporting that nearly 40% of surveyed clinicians use AI for summaries of research and standards of care. However, this may be done with limited visibility into how those systems were built, tested, or constrained. The tools exist. The adoption is happening. The missing piece, in most cases, is the evaluation rigor that should precede clinician usage.
At Abridge, we believe that enterprise AI in healthcare must be trustworthy at scale, and that starts with being transparent about our evaluation processes and guardrails.

sourceContent.headline: How Deaconess psychiatric nurse practitioner uses context-aware decision support
sourceContent.description: Learn how nurse practitioner Olivia Taylor at Deaconess Health is using Abridge's context-aware decision support in her practice.
paragraphs: We sat down with Olivia Taylor, a psychiatric mental health nurse practitioner at Deaconess Health with a decade of experience across both inpatient and outpatient care.
And if you're curious how Abridge's context-aware decision support could fit into your workflow, head to the CDS page on our website to learn more.
It's made me noticeably more efficient, without giving up the evidence-based care I pride myself in using.

Psychiatric care requires a high degree of personalization that balances clinical rigor with a respect for humanity. Clinicians need deep knowledge of medications, interactions, and treatment approaches while continually assessing what patients report and how their symptoms, behavior, and functioning change over time. Treatment decisions depend on bringing together the patient’s story and the latest evidence, with room for adjustment at any time.

Abridge's clinical intelligence provides evidence at the point of care, contextualized to the patient in the room. It leverages the patient conversation alongside information from the electronic health record—including prior notes, labs, diagnoses, and other chart data—to shape the evidence it surfaces during care. No switching tabs. No digging for labs. Just evidence-based insights, tailored to each patient's clinical situation, now implemented enterprise-wide at more than 300 health systems.

We sat down with Olivia Taylor, a psychiatric mental health nurse practitioner at Deaconess Health with a decade of experience across both inpatient and outpatient care. In our conversation, she shared how Abridge's clinical intelligence has changed her day-to-day workflow, a recent example of how she used it with a patient to support her recommendation on tapering a medication, and the relief she experienced after a day of helping people through “some of the hardest moments of their lives.”

paragraphs: Built by clinicians and machine learning scientists working side by side, it's trained to weigh what matters the way a clinician would: the allergy that rules out a drug, the family history that moves a screening up, the guideline exception this patient meets.
As a practicing primary care clinician, she's using Abridge Assistant's context-aware decision support across her own workflow.
In our conversation, she shared how Abridge Assistant has transformed her practice before, during, and after visits, and where she sees Abridge having the greatest impact.

Primary care requires clinicians to have an enormous range of knowledge. A single day's schedule might run from seeing a newborn for their first checkup to managing a chronic condition for a geriatric patient, and each carries its own set of guidelines, screening intervals, and medication considerations. Much of the work of preparing for that day happens outside of the exam room.

Abridge Assistant brings contextual clinical reasoning to the point of care. Built by clinicians and machine learning scientists working side by side, it's trained to weigh what matters the way a clinician would: the allergy that rules out a drug, the family history that moves a screening up, the guideline exception this patient meets. It draws on the conversation, the chart, and trusted medical literature to deliver evidence-based responses without pulling you out of your workflow. Now live across more than 300 health systems, and getting sharper with every capability clinicians ask for.

We recently sat down with Dr. Kristin Jacob, an internal medicine-pediatrics clinician and Medical Director of Physician and APP Well-Being at Corewell Health. As a practicing primary care clinician, she's using Abridge Assistant's context-aware decision support across her own workflow. As a well-being leader, she's also thinking about how to bring it to the colleagues who stand to benefit most. In our conversation, she shared how Abridge Assistant has transformed her practice before, during, and after visits, and where she sees Abridge having the greatest impact.

sourceContent.headline: How WVU Emergency Medicine Clinician Uses Context-Aware Decision Support
sourceContent.description: Learn how emergency medicine clinician Dr. Brian Dilcher at West Virginia University Medicine uses Abridge's context-aware decision support.
paragraphs: How does it hold up in an environment as fast-moving as the ED?
I work mostly in the adult ED, with a shift or two a quarter in the pediatric ED.
In high-pressure care settings like the emergency department, time and information are everything, but in scarce supply.

In high-pressure care settings like the emergency department, time and information are everything, but in scarce supply. Clinicians must immediately assess problems and make decisions, all while new patients continue to arrive. There is rarely time to consult all of the latest, most-relevant literature and guidance. And new evidence is published at an impossible clip.

Abridge's clinical intelligence provides evidence at the point of care, contextualized to the patient in the room. It leverages the patient conversation alongside information from the electronic health record—including prior notes, labs, diagnoses, and other chart data—to shape the evidence it surfaces during care. No switching tabs. No digging for labs. Just evidence-based insights, tailored to each patient's clinical situation, now implemented enterprise-wide at more than 300 health systems.

We sat down with Dr. Brian Dilcher, an emergency medicine clinician and associate Chief Medical Information Officer (CMIO) for emergency medicine at WVU Medicine’s Ruby Memorial Hospital in West Virginia. As an informatics leader, he decides whether technologies like Abridge are rigorous enough to meet the needs of fellow clinicians and residents. As a practicing clinician, he's also the one using it, so he has a personal stake. In our conversation, he shared how he’s using Abridge’s clinical intelligence in his own practice and how it's earned his trust as both a clinician and an informatics leader.

Multiple teams within the same company increasingly need shared access to expensive GPU clusters for their generative AI operations, while maintaining isolation boundaries, resource fairness, and operational independence. Consider a data science team training large language models, a computer vision group running inference workloads, and a research team experimenting with new model architectures. All of them might need access to the same cluster. Without a well-designed multi-tenant (multi-team) architecture, organizations face uncontrolled resource consumption, weak isolation between teams, an inability to attribute shared GPU costs to the teams that incur them, and administrative overhead that slows down innovation.

Amazon SageMaker HyperPod is a purpose-built AI service that simplifies the management of large-scale compute clusters for gen AI workloads. It provides resilient, optimized clusters orchestrated by Amazon Elastic Kubernetes Service (Amazon EKS) or Slurm, so organizations can run distributed training, interactive development, and model inference at scale. At the same time, it automatically handles node health monitoring, fault recovery, and cluster lifecycle management.

In this post, we present a reference architecture for building a multi-tenant environment on Amazon SageMaker HyperPod with EKS. This architecture uses AWS IAM Identity Center for centralized authentication, per-team SageMaker AI domains for a tailored user experience, Kubernetes namespaces for workload isolation, HyperPod Task Governance for fair resource allocation, and namespace-level cost allocation for per-team spend visibility and chargeback. By the end of this post, you will have a clear blueprint for multiple teams to efficiently share a single HyperPod EKS cluster.
