articles.title: Why I tried to kill token billing (and why we kept it)
articles.descEn: Token billing is useful infrastructure, but usually a bad customer-facing pricing model. Your invoice should define the value your product delivers, not break down what it cost you to create it.
articles.titleEn: Why I tried to kill token billing (and why we kept it)
summaryLinesEn: For model providers, token usage is the product.
They make model-routing decisions upstream, then send the resulting token usage to Metronome—either broken out by customer or attributed to a single aggregate customer for cost tracking.
In its simplest form, passthrough pricing charges customers for the model tokens their usage consumes, plus a markup on the underlying cost.

sourceContent.headline: Why I tried to kill token billing (and why we kept it)
sourceContent.description: Token billing is useful infrastructure, but usually a bad customer-facing pricing model. Your invoice should define the value your product delivers, not break down what it cost you to create it.
paragraphs: For model providers, token usage is the product.
They make model-routing decisions upstream, then send the resulting token usage to Metronome—either broken out by customer or attributed to a single aggregate customer for cost tracking.
In its simplest form, passthrough pricing charges customers for the model tokens their usage consumes, plus a markup on the underlying cost.

Token billing is useful infrastructure and, for almost every company, a bad customer-facing pricing model. In its simplest form, passthrough pricing charges customers for the model tokens their usage consumes, plus a markup on the underlying cost. If you’re building your pricing around that token consumption, you’re letting your costs determine your price.

That’s reflected in how our customers are using token billing today. They need it on the backend to track usage, manage markups, and protect their unit economics, but they don’t want those details defining how they price their product.
This gets at something I’ve been saying for a while: your invoice should be where you define your value to your customer.

articles.title: Introducing Speech (beta)
articles.descEn: A new way to express yourself creatively
articles.titleEn: Introducing Speech (beta)
summaryLinesEn: Speech opens up another canvas for that same kind of creativity.

Every day, people make songs for birthdays, weddings, inside jokes, faith and worship, their kids, their friends, and moments that might mean absolutely nothing to anyone else but mean everything to them.
Today, we’re expanding what's possible in Suno with Speech : the first audio model that generates voice and music together as one cohesive track.

Today, we’re expanding what's possible in Suno with Speech : the first audio model that generates voice and music together as one cohesive track.

As new technologies make creation more accessible, more people can experience the joy of turning an idea into music, a story, or art, and get fulfillment from the simple act of making something. We call that creative entertainment , and we think it will define the next wave of consumer technology.

Music will always be at the heart of Suno and what we build. At the same time, our vision has always extended to other forms of human expression. Today, we’re expanding what's possible in Suno with Speech : the first audio model that generates voice and music together as one cohesive track.

Speech lets you create spoken audio set to original background music. It's built right into Suno: type an idea, a poem or something you've written, then describe the voice and musical style you have in mind.

articles.title: How NVIDIA GPUs Help Accelerate OpenAI’s GPT-6 Astra Ultrafast
articles.descEn: Running on NVIDIA Blackwell GPUs and accelerated by continuous inference optimizations through OpenAI’s models, GPT-6 Astra Ultrafast delivers faster model responses across code generation, tool use and interactive applications.
articles.titleEn: How NVIDIA GPUs Help Accelerate OpenAI’s GPT-6 Astra Ultrafast
summaryLinesEn: “NVIDIA’s deep investment in tooling and documentation has enabled us to make our models exceptionally good at programming Blackwell and Rubin GPUs,” said Philippe Tillet, inference lead at OpenAI.

Accelerated by inference optimizations through OpenAI’s models that tap into the capabilities of the NVIDIA Blackwell architecture, Ultrafast offers up to 8x faster token generation than the Astra Standard mode.
OpenAI is using its own models to help refine the inference software running on NVIDIA GPUs, taking advantage of the platform’s programmability to test and implement improvements.

sourceContent.headline: How NVIDIA GPUs Help Accelerate OpenAI’s GPT-6 Astra Ultrafast
sourceContent.description: Running on NVIDIA Blackwell GPUs and accelerated by continuous inference optimizations through OpenAI’s models, GPT-6 Astra Ultrafast delivers faster model responses across code generation, tool use and interactive applications.
paragraphs: “NVIDIA’s deep investment in tooling and documentation has enabled us to make our models exceptionally good at programming Blackwell and Rubin GPUs,” said Philippe Tillet, inference lead at OpenAI.

Accelerated by inference optimizations through OpenAI’s models that tap into the capabilities of the NVIDIA Blackwell architecture, Ultrafast offers up to 8x faster token generation than the Astra Standard mode.
OpenAI is using its own models to help refine the inference software running on NVIDIA GPUs, taking advantage of the platform’s programmability to test and implement improvements.
GPT-6 Astra Ultrafast, running on NVIDIA Blackwell GPUs , is available now in the OpenAI API and to eligible ChatGPT Work and Codex users.

Accelerated by inference optimizations through OpenAI’s models that tap into the capabilities of the NVIDIA Blackwell architecture, Ultrafast offers up to 8x faster token generation than the Astra Standard mode. For developers, faster generation can shorten coding agents’ edit-test-debug cycles, reduce the time spent generating responses between tool calls and make interactive applications feel more responsive.

A faster response matters most when it’s repeated across a workflow: an agent writes code, uses a tool, checks the result and decides what to do next. Ultrafast brings Astra’s capabilities into these time-sensitive loops. NVIDIA AI infrastructure helps OpenAI serve more useful model outputs when developers need it.

summaryLines: OpenAI의 추론 책임자인 Philippe Tillet은 "NVIDIA는 도구 및 문서화에 대한 깊은 투자를 통해 Blackwell 및 Rubin GPU 프로그래밍에 탁월한 모델을 만들 수 있었음" · 라고 말함

articles.descEn: Google's tensor processing units were launched into orbit on Planet Labs satellites.
articles.titleEn: SpaceX launches Google AI chips into orbit in push toward space-based data centers
summaryLinesEn: The Transporter-18 mission marks the first in-orbit test for Alphabet's Project Suncatcher, ​a "moonshot" initiative to develop reliable AI computing infrastructure in space.
Alphabet launched its homegrown AI chips into orbit on Thursday in a SpaceX Falcon 9 rocket, a step towards making data centers in space a reality.
Industry experts say space-based data centers represent a far-out mission, if they can even become feasible, in part because rocket launches remain capacity-constrained and expensive.

Today, we’re announcing the public preview of AWS Well-Architected Agent , an AI-powered service that analyzes your AWS environment to deliver targeted, contextual recommendations for improving your applications’ cost, security, performance, and resilience. The AWS Well-Architected Agent analyzes your infrastructure, understands unique business goals, and delivers contextual recommendations with ready-to-implement fixes. It delivers context-aware optimization without relying on manual audits or generic checklists.

The agent evaluates your environment as an experienced cloud architect would. It automatically correlates utilization metrics, resource configurations, and application topology, and analyzes against Well-Architected best practices across 65+ AWS services. It generates recommendations aligned to your declared business goals, delivers implementation packages with every finding, and surfaces cross-pillar trade-offs making it simpler to remediate the findings.

Goal-aligned intelligence : AWS Well-Architected Agent replaces flat, undifferentiated findings with context-aware, prioritized recommendations. articles.title: SynthID Bio: Watermarking methods for synthetic biology
articles.descEn: SynthID Bio is a family of watermarking methods developed specifically for synthetic biology to strengthen biosecurity and scientific integrity.
articles.titleEn: SynthID Bio: Watermarking methods for synthetic biology
summaryLinesEn: SynthID Bio preserves AlphaFold 3 prediction accuracy while offering near-perfect detectability, maintaining key structural feature distributions, and holding up against digital noise or minor coordinate changes.

Yet these tools also present new challenges: novel AI designs can bypass traditional DNA synthesis screening, while mislabeled synthetic 3D structures risk polluting public databases and misleading downstream research.
Today, we’re introducing SynthID Bio to bring watermarking technology to synthetic biology.

articles.title: D4RT: Unified, Fast 4D Scene Reconstruction & Tracking
articles.descEn: Meet D4RT, a unified AI model for 4D scene reconstruction and tracking.
articles.titleEn: D4RT: Unified, Fast 4D Scene Reconstruction & Tracking
summaryLinesEn: Previous state-of-the-art methods could take up to ten minutes for the same task — an improvement of 120x.

Today, we are introducing D4RT (Dynamic 4D Reconstruction and Tracking) , a new AI model that unifies dynamic scene reconstruction into a single, efficient framework, bringing us closer to the next frontier of artificial intelligence: total perception of our dynamic reality.

D4RT’s simplified architecture and novel query mechanism place it at the forefront of 4D reconstruction while being up to 300x more efficient than previous methods — fast enough for real-time applications in robotics, augmented reality, and more.

sourceContent.description: Meet D4RT, a unified AI model for 4D scene reconstruction and tracking.
paragraphs: Previous state-of-the-art methods could take up to ten minutes for the same task — an improvement of 120x.

Today, we are introducing D4RT (Dynamic 4D Reconstruction and Tracking) , a new AI model that unifies dynamic scene reconstruction into a single, efficient framework, bringing us closer to the next frontier of artificial intelligence: total perception of our dynamic reality.

D4RT’s simplified architecture and novel query mechanism place it at the forefront of 4D reconstruction while being up to 300x more efficient than previous methods — fast enough for real-time applications in robotics, augmented reality, and more.
Introducing D4RT, a unified AI model for 4D scene reconstruction and tracking across space and time.

Anytime we look at the world, we perform an extraordinary feat of memory and prediction. We see and understand things as they are at a given moment in time, as they were a moment ago, and how they are going to be in the moment to follow. Our mental model of the world maintains a persistent representation of reality and we use that model to draw intuitive conclusions about the causal relationship between the past, present and future.

To help machines see the world more like we do, we can equip them with cameras, but that only solves the problem of input. To make sense of this input, computers must solve a complex, inverse problem: taking a video — which is a sequence of flat 2D projections — and recovering or understanding the rich, volumetric 3D world, in motion.
sourceContent.text:
Previous state-of-the-art methods could take up to ten minutes for the same task — an improvement of 120x.

Today, we are introducing D4RT (Dynamic 4D Reconstruction and Tracking) , a new AI model that unifies dynamic scene reconstruction into a single, efficient framework, bringing us closer to the next frontier of artificial intelligence: total perception of our dynamic reality.

D4RT’s simplified architecture and novel query mechanism place it at the forefront of 4D reconstruction while being up to 300x more efficient than previous methods — fast enough for real-time applications in robotics, augmented reality, and more.

Introducing D4RT, a unified AI model for 4D scene reconstruction and tracking across space and time.

Anytime we look at the world, we perform an extraordinary feat of memory and prediction. We see and understand things as they are at a given moment in time, as they were a moment ago, and how they are going to be in the moment to follow. Our mental model of the world maintains a persistent representation of reality and we use that model to draw intuitive conclusions about the causal relationship between the past, present and future.

To help machines see the world more like we do, we can equip them with cameras, but that only solves the problem of input. To make sense of this input, computers must solve a complex, inverse problem: taking a video — which is a sequence of flat 2D projections — and recovering or understanding the rich, volumetric 3D world, in motion.

articles.descEn: We’re on a journey to advance and democratize artificial intelligence through open source and open science.
articles.titleEn: Open TTS Leaderboard: Scalable Evaluation for Multilingual Text-to-Speech and Voice Cloning
summaryLinesEn: The goal of the Open TTS Leaderboard is not only to keep up with the incredible pace of TTS model releases, but to be shaped by the community; we want to hear your feedback so the evaluations stay relevant and insightful.
By toggling “Voice cloning”, the models that support this functionality (on the selected languages) can be compared.

This may partly explain why open-source models are underrepresented on arena-style leaderboards: as of Sep 30, 2026, only 16 of the 92 models on Artificial Analysis are open-weights, with a similar skew on Voice Arena .

Today, support for Open USD (OUSD) launches across Stripe products. OUSD is a new stablecoin from Open Standard that is designed for global money movement at scale and enables any business to transact and build with internet-native payment rails.

Businesses can now use OUSD to receive, hold, send, and spend funds with Treasury; build and operate a global card program with Issuing; and pay recipients globally with Global Payouts . Businesses can also offer fiat-to-OUSD conversions to their customers with Crypto Onramp and accept OUSD with Payments .

paragraphs: Learn how Microsoft Circular Centers are scaling cloud supply chain sustainability .

Responsible infrastructure at hyperscale: Managing the full lifecycle of Azure hardware
Every new generation of cloud infrastructure creates two jobs. We must deploy more capable systems quickly, and we must manage the hardware they replace responsibly.

Even though these jobs happen behind the scenes, the results matter to Microsoft Azure customers. Newer systems deliver more compute capacity from the space and power available in a datacenter. At the same time, the reuse, refurbishment, and recycling of older equipment can extend the life of valuable components and return materials to the supply chain, ensuring cost efficiency and reliability.

Amazon is developing AI-powered smart glasses to help streamline work for its delivery drivers.
As Amazon continues its rollout of AI smart glasses, privacy concerns are growing.

A few days ago, I crossed paths with an Amazon delivery driver who was wearing some odd-looking glasses. I paused, wondering if it was a pair of the new AI smart glasses ( I reported on them last year ) or if he just had questionable taste in eyewear. After Wednesday’s news, my curiosity has evolved into concern.

In a Bloomberg opinion piece, reporter Dave Lee shared his thoughts on the new AI smart glasses based on an interview with Amazon executive Viraj Chatterjee, who is spearheading the rollout. According to the report, Amazon aims to have 5,000 drivers wearing the glasses by the end of 2026, expanding to more than 20,000 by the end of 2027.

FREMONT, Calif., Sept. 30, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- ACM Research, Inc. ("ACM") (NASDAQ: ACMR), a leading supplier of wafer and panel processing solutions for semiconductor and advanced packaging applications, today announced that its operating subsidiary, ACM Research (Shanghai), Inc. ("ACM Shanghai") posted backlog figures for ACM Shanghai as of September 29, 2026 on the Shanghai Stock Exchange website [ link to China Disclosure ].

As of September 29, 2026, ACM Shanghai's total backlog amounted to RMB 17.1 billion (USD $2.5 billion), an 88.2% year-over-year increase compared with the prior year's disclosed backlog. The total backlog figures include a mix of orders for tools that have been shipped but not yet recognized as revenue under Chinese generally accepted accounting principles ("Chinese GAAP"), and orders for tools expected to be shipped at a future date.

summaryLinesEn: Some of the most optimistic analysts saw Cisco reaching about US$90.6b in revenue and US$23.0b in earnings by 2029, so this Bell Canada AI deal could either reinforce that AI cycle story or expose how dependent those bullish forecasts are on hyperscalers and sovereign projects actually sustaining their current pace.

The Bell Canada sovereign AI MOU reinforces the AI and regulated‑sector demand story, but it does not materially change the near term gross margin headwind or the risk that investors reassess Cisco's growth and earnings multiple.

NEW YORK, Sept. 30, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- AIB Data Centers Inc. (NYSE American: AIB) ("AIB" or the "Company"), a developer and operator of purpose-built data centers for artificial intelligence and high-performance computing, today announced that it has entered into a binding agreement with Nebius (Nasdaq: NBIS), the AI cloud company, for 50 MW of critical IT capacity at AIB's facility located in the southeastern United States.

articles.title: Instagram is adding an AI ‘assistant’ to tell you how to post
articles.descEn: Instagram will tell creators what’s working and what’s not — along with AI-generated suggestions on how to change their content.
articles.titleEn: Instagram is adding an AI ‘assistant’ to tell you how to post
summaryLinesEn: Tools like CrowdTangle, which researchers and journalists used to monitor the most popular content on Meta platforms , have been shut down or restricted .

The shift also raises interesting new questions about the relationship between tech companies and the creators that fill the platforms with things to look at: How does this dynamic change when platforms are straightforwardly giving creators instructions on how to post?
If that sounds familiar, it’s because YouTube also just announced updates to its sprawling AI-powered dashboard that tells creators how to maximize engagement.

summaryLines: 연구원과 저널리스트가 메타 플랫폼에서 가장 인기 있는 콘텐츠를 모니터링하는 데 사용했던 CrowdTangle과 같은 도구는 종료되거나 제한됨
이러한 변화는 또한 기술 회사와 플랫폼을 살펴볼 내용으로 채우는 제작자 간의 관계에 대한 흥미롭고 새로운 질문을 제기함 · 플랫폼이 제작자에게 게시 방법에 대한 지침을 직접 제공할 때 이러한 역동적인 변화는 어떻게 이루어 집니까
익숙하게 들린다면 YouTube가 제작자에게 참여를 극대화하는 방법을 알려주는 광범위한 AI 기반 대시보드에 대한 업데이트도 방금 발표했기 때문임

articles.title: OpenAI is sued over rogue AI Hugging Face cyberattack
articles.descEn: The lawsuit appears to be the first publicly reported case seeking to hold an AI developer liable for an incident caused by rogue systems.
articles.titleEn: OpenAI is sued over rogue AI Hugging Face cyberattack
summaryLinesEn: Nvidia announced it had agreed to pay roughly $13 billion to buy Hugging Face earlier this month.
CEO Clément Delangue previously said in July he asked OpenAI to commit $100 million in compute "to help the Hugging Face community build powerful cyber defenses with the best open and closed models."
OpenAI had tried to invest $100 million into the startup after the cyberattack, though talks fell apart in the early stages, sources told CNBC.

paragraphs: Nvidia announced it had agreed to pay roughly $13 billion to buy Hugging Face earlier this month.
CEO Clément Delangue previously said in July he asked OpenAI to commit $100 million in compute "to help the Hugging Face community build powerful cyber defenses with the best open and closed models."
OpenAI had tried to invest $100 million into the startup after the cyberattack, though talks fell apart in the early stages, sources told CNBC.
OpenAI has been sued over a cyberattack its models committed against startup Hugging Face in July.
The lawsuit, filed by a non-profit, appears to be the first publicly reported case seeking to hold an AI developer liable for an incident caused by rogue systems.
The Hugging Face cyberattack prompted numerous admissions from other AI labs about rogue AI agents causing security incidents.

summaryLines: 엔비디아는 이번 달 초 Hugging Face를 인수하기 위해 약 130억 달러를 지불하기로 합의했다고 발표함
CEO Clément Delangue는 이전에 지난 7월 OpenAI에 "Hugging Face 커뮤니티가 최고의 개방형 및 폐쇄형 모델을 사용하여 강력한 사이버 방어를 구축할 수 있도록 돕기 위해" 컴퓨팅에 1억 달러를 투자하도록 요청했다고 밝힘
OpenAI는 사이버 공격 이후 스타트업에 1억 달러를 투자하려 했으나 초기 단계에서 논의가 결렬되었다고 소식통은 CNBC에 말함

DUBAI, UAE, Sept. 30, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Flytxt , a global provider of Enterprise AI for subscription businesses, today announced that it has been recognised as a Challenger in the 2026 Gartner® Magic Quadrant™ for CSP AI-Enabled Marketing and Sales Solutions .

Flytxt views this positioning as a progression from its recognition as a Niche Player in 2025 , reflecting the company's continued growth and strong competitive position in the CSP AI market. It comes amid an expanding global footprint, broader coverage of AI-enabled marketing and sales use cases, and sustained investment in enterprise AI capabilities designed to drive business outcomes at scale.

"We view our inclusion in a Gartner Magic Quadrant for the third time, and our positioning as a Challenger this year, as an affirmation of our pioneering work in enterprise AI," said Dr. Vinod Vasudevan, CEO, Flytxt. "Our vision is to move beyond Co-pilots and task automation agents by creating an AI Expertforce that combines domain intelligence with agentic execution to autonomously drive growth and marketplace efficiency for CSPs."

summaryLinesEn: Use ai_decide when you need fast, low-cost decisions over governed data: routing prompts to the right model, tagging customer reviews with metadata, or evaluating agent quality—at batch scale in SQL or in real-time over REST.

articles.descEn: Apple's absence from Trump's AI lunch raised eyebrows, but the company is known to look out for its own interests.

summaryLinesEn: Apple's stock is up 22.5% so far in 2026, outpacing the Nasdaq and almost all of its megacap peers other than Nvidia, which is up about the same amount.

President Donald Trump's gathering of the world's most powerful tech companies didn't include one notable company: Apple.
Former CEO Tim Cook now acts as Apple's public face with government officials around the world, and he maintains a good relationship with Trump.
While every other major U.S. tech company was represented, Altimeter Capital CEO Brad Gerstner called Apple's absence a "nothing burger."

articles.title: How can I help to protect my kids from inappropriate internet content using parental controls?
articles.descEn: Learn how parental controls can help manage the content your kids can access, support internet safety for kids and limit exposure to inappropriate internet content.
articles.titleEn: How can I help to protect my kids from inappropriate internet content using parental controls?
summaryLinesEn: Knowing how to set up parental controls is only the first step — as kids get older, the apps they use, the people they communicate with and the content that’s appropriate for them will change.

If they move from the TV to a tablet or game console, Fios Router controls can help keep the same content filters, schedules and daily internet limits in place across the devices assigned to their profile.

Adding blocks and filters can help you reduce access to inappropriate websites, apps and other content, but parents should combine them with age-appropriate settings and ongoing conversations about what kids may encounter online.

articles.title: Helping personal agents shop more intelligently and reliably with Link
articles.descEn: As agents take on more purchases, agent builders have increasingly asked us to help agents navigate checkout and earn consumer trust. Today, we’re sharing three major improvements to support this broader set of needs.
articles.titleEn: Helping personal agents shop more intelligently and reliably with Link
summaryLinesEn: The most popular personal AI agents—such as Muse, Meta’s new personal agent; Grok Bot; and Instinct—now use Link’s wallet for agents to power consumer spending.

Link can now help agents complete more purchases with incremental authorization and guidance on how to overcome checkout obstacles; analyze consumer spending to make better product recommendations; and provide purchase protection if an agent makes a mistake.
Consumers are embracing this new way to shop: over the past month, agentic purchases made with Link increased 38x.

articles.descEn: Seven updates that capture complexity at the point of care, give admins more control over Abridge, and deepen specialty support.
articles.titleEn: Abridge September 2026 Release: Inpatient Cues, New Specialty Support, & More
summaryLinesEn: Two updates this month give project and CDI teams more direct control over their Abridge implementation.
This builds on Abridge’s Query Engine, introduced in July, which surfaces AAPC-compliant CDI queries inline in the note when a documentation gap is present.
Because the prompt arrives while the context is still fresh, the full complexity of the care makes it into the chart, and clinicians can have more confidence that nothing was left out.

sourceContent.headline: Abridge September 2026 Release: Inpatient Cues, New Specialty Support, & More
sourceContent.description: Seven updates that capture complexity at the point of care, give admins more control over Abridge, and deepen specialty support.
paragraphs: Two updates this month give project and CDI teams more direct control over their Abridge implementation.
This builds on Abridge’s Query Engine, introduced in July, which surfaces AAPC-compliant CDI queries inline in the note when a documentation gap is present.
Because the prompt arrives while the context is still fresh, the full complexity of the care makes it into the chart, and clinicians can have more confidence that nothing was left out.

Welcome back to Now in Practice. One throughline in this month’s release is the timing and detail behind how complex care makes it into the record. Diagnoses organized and refined while the clinician is still in the note. Related conditions grouped together so combination codes can surface before the chart closes. Cues that capture what was discussed during an inpatient stay while the story is still fresh.

So much of what often comes back weeks later as a retrospective query was known in the moment, and each of these updates is a version of the same goal: settling that detail at the point of care so the record reflects the full complexity of the care delivered and holds up on review. Alongside them, two updates give administrators more direct control over their Abridge implementation, and two specialty model enhancements now capture the details that define allergy and palliative care.

Three capabilities in this release are focused on closing the gap between the care delivered and the care that is documented: the diagnosis that’s accurate but not specific enough, the combination code split across a flat list, and the observation made at the bedside that never reaches the note.

sourceContent.description: Run SQL Server on Azure Local. Bring cloud-connected management, disconnected operations, and local AI to your sovereign data environments.
paragraphs: Updates July 14 5 min read SQL Server 2016 end of support is here: Plan your next steps See what changes as SQL Server 2016 reaches end of support.
Today, SQL Server on Azure Local is generally available for connected and disconnected operations.
As of September 29, 2026, Foundry Local on Azure Local is currently available in preview, so availability and capabilities may change before general availability.

Some of the world’s most critical databases run in places where cloud connectivity cannot be assumed. A remote industrial site, for example, may need production systems to continue operating when external connectivity is unavailable. A regulated organization may need sensitive data and processing to remain within sovereign boundaries.

Today, SQL Server on Azure Local is generally available for connected and disconnected operations. With this release, customers can modernize where their data resides while maintaining control over infrastructure, connectivity, and data placement. They can bring AI closer to their data with Foundry Local on Azure Local , currently in preview, and use eligible existing SQL Server licensing investments.

SQL Server has a long history of supporting mission-critical workloads on customer infrastructure. Azure Local builds on that flexibility by bringing Azure infrastructure to customer-owned environments, giving organizations a consistent platform for running SQL Server across datacenters and edge locations.

articles.title: Three Must-learn Tips for Using EQ
articles.descEn: EQ will be one of the first tools to master when you come to Suno Studio. Get started here!
articles.titleEn: Three Must-learn Tips for Using EQ
summaryLinesEn: You first instinct might be to turn up the high-mids and treble for a bit more presence.
Suno Studio has had EQ per track since it launched in 2025.

Digital audio has a theoretical maximum (0dBFS) meaning everything you add, including gain from your various EQ bands, will need to find a space in your master bus: the combination of all your tracks and effects.

Digital audio has a theoretical maximum (0dBFS) meaning everything you add, including gain from your various EQ bands, will need to find a space in your master bus: the combination of all your tracks and effects.

In a previous blogpost, I said that compression was one of the most ubiquitous music production tools. And while this is true, there is a clear winner in this particular popularity contest. And the winner is: Equalization , normally referred to as EQ . You’ll find EQ everywhere in music production.
Some DAWs, like Logic Pro, have EQ built into every channel, whether you want it or not, ready to grab at a moment's notice. The truth is you normally will want to use it.

Seasoned producers will often have several go-to EQs; I for one love to grab Ableton Live’s EQ Three for crude tone shaping, and EQ Eight for fine tuning. But if I want some character, I’ll go for a Pultec, API or SSL emulation to give my tracks more bite.

summaryLinesEn: AI giants' IPOs, chipmaker AMD said Monday it is acquiring World Labs for $8.2 billion in a stock deal.

When OpenAI hired OpenClaw founder Peter Steinberger to head the company’s agentic AI developments, I’d suspected we’d be in for some big agent news at OpenAI’s annual DevDay on Tuesday. Enter dots.

We’re talking about always-on, autonomous agents powered by the company’s GPT-6 Astra AI model and designed to handle any task. Dots can connect to more than 4,000 apps and can integrate with ChatGPT, Slack or Teams to handle work assignments, according to the company’s blog post . You’ll be able to access dots in ChatGPT on desktop, web and mobile.

summaryLinesEn: That is not to say that every expert has thrown up their hands.
The agents have broken our control, the body said, and even reining them in now will not guarantee our collective ability to corral them later.

articles.descEn: Adobe, Freeport-McMoRan, Kyndryl, and Salesforce are learning that making AI agents pay off requires fewer, more targeted deployments; rigorous outcome-based measurement; and business teams willing to redesign workflows from scratch.
articles.titleEn: Agentic AI early adopters have failed, pivoted, and learned these 3 lessons | Fortune
summaryLinesEn: According to White, the new agentic process increased the proportion of cases being resolved and routed to the right group the first time from 12% to 34%, saving the firm over $350,000 in a year.

Salesforce—which sells the same agentic AI systems it’s using internally as its products—similarly pivoted from hundreds of agents to a few the company strongly believed could deliver specific benefits, according to SVP Andy White, who oversees adoption of Salesforce products for internal operations.

paragraphs: According to White, the new agentic process increased the proportion of cases being resolved and routed to the right group the first time from 12% to 34%, saving the firm over $350,000 in a year.

Salesforce—which sells the same agentic AI systems it’s using internally as its products—similarly pivoted from hundreds of agents to a few the company strongly believed could deliver specific benefits, according to SVP Andy White, who oversees adoption of Salesforce products for internal operations.

In 2026, AI agents went from shiny object to top priority for enterprises, with 74% of leaders now expecting nearly half of their business processes to be redesigned around AI agents within four years, according to a Deloitte survey on agentic transformation published in August. Yet only 16% of respondents said they’re prepared.

As part of the 2026 AIQ 75 list, Fortune set out to find companies that are deep into rolling out AI agents and automating workflows at scale. This year’s survey included several new questions focused specifically on agentic AI use within companies.

Among the companies that ranked highest for agentic AI, Adobe , Freeport-McMoRan , Kyndryl, and Salesforce opened up about the ins and outs of their experiences thus far. They’re broadly tapping agentic AI for everything from invoicing to product research, software engineering, and both employee and customer help desks. These companies have all failed, pivoted, and made real progress, and they all came to the same conclusions: You have to work toward solving a specific business problem; bring tech and business stakeholders together; and focus relentlessly on ROI.

summaryLinesEn: Applied Materials (AMAT) stock has climbed more than 96% year-to-date (YTD), supported by robust artificial intelligence (AI)-related demand for advanced semiconductors and the equipment required to manufacture them.

sourceContent.headline: Travel’s AI dilemma at Skift Global Forum
sourceContent.description: At the annual travel conference, Airbnb CEO Brian Chesky called AI “an existential risk” to his company and “literally the best thing to ever happen” to it in the same discussion. That sums up many travel leaders’ push-and-pull relationship with AI.
paragraphs: Meanwhile, Radar, Stripe’s AI-powered fraud prevention tool, blocked the overwhelming majority of those attempts—the share of attempted fraud that reached the payment stage fell by more than two-thirds from 2023 to 2025.
It assesses risk signals such as dispute likelihood, card testing, stolen-card risk, and issuer-decline patterns.

Executives from Expedia Group, Priceline, IHG Hotels & Resorts, Amadeus, and other companies discussed how to harness the benefits of AI—more personalized discovery, faster customer service, new sources of revenue—without giving up control of the booking or their brand.

At the Skift Global Forum last week, a conference themed around the travel industry’s “great recalibration,” Airbnb CEO Brian Chesky effectively summed up attendees’ push-and-pull relationship with AI. At different points in his roughly 30-minute conversation onstage Wednesday, Chesky called AI “an existential risk” to his company and “literally the best thing to ever happen” to it. AI could threaten Airbnb’s hold on travel discovery, but Chesky also credits the technology with helping his team ship nearly twice as many features as last year.

That contradiction surfaced throughout the three-day event, which brought nearly 1,000 travel leaders from 45 countries to New York. Executives from Expedia Group, Priceline, IHG Hotels & Resorts, Amadeus, and other companies discussed how to harness the benefits of AI—more personalized discovery, faster customer service, new sources of revenue—without giving up control of the booking or their brand.

A central question was whether AI will simplify travel or fragment it further. For now, it’s doing both: simplifying individual tasks like comparing options or changing a booking, and multiplying the agents, interfaces, and paths travelers use to plan and purchase a trip. Travel leaders are making decisions in real time about which agents to partner with, what to build themselves, and how to preserve the integrity of customer relationships in what Amadeus Executive Vice President Elena Avila called a “high emotion, high stakes” industry.

articles.titleEn: Ghostwriter: When AI goes from tool to teammate
summaryLinesEn: But Ghostwriter isn’t DMing you on Slack when it thinks your AI agent’s sales promotion’s lost its effectiveness.

If you’ve tried Instinct or Muse , you may have had that moment: Wait, it noticed that? Your agent spots something you missed, figures out what to do, and comes back with a solution. Maybe it catches a change to your flight and finds a better option before you’ve even opened the airline app. The first time that happens, it changes how you think about AI. This agent is not just a tool, it’s got my back .

In the business world, we’ve been marching in this direction, but haven’t quite gotten all the way there. Agents are writing almost all code but they’re not yet tapping developers on the shoulder with feature ideas or an A/B test to run. With Sierra’s Ghostwriter , our customers have transitioned from code to clicks to prompts , dramatically speeding up how they build and deploy agents. But Ghostwriter isn’t DMing you on Slack when it thinks your AI agent’s sales promotion’s lost its effectiveness. Until today.

articles.titleEn: Introducing the new Copilot with Home, Code and Autopilot - The Official Microsoft Blog
summaryLinesEn: From Home you can ask Copilot to draft a launch brief, model a budget, build a deck, or pick up a file your team is already working on, and it creates or updates a real, editable document, workbook or presentation — live for your whole team, not just you.

Sep 25, 2026 | Jared Spataro - Chief Marketing Officer, AI at Work

We’re reimagining Microsoft Copilot to enable work as it evolves and to help expand what every individual and every organization can accomplish in the flow of human ambition. Today we’re introducing the new Copilot to connect the tools people rely on with the next generation of capabilities they’ll need to build, customize and scale AI across work.

The Copilot app now has three new capabilities: Home is your new starting point, where Chat and Cowork come together — and with Office in Copilot , the full power of Word, Excel and PowerPoint is now built into the experience. Code lets everyone build their own solutions with the tools to run them safely, and it’s powered by the same underlying technology as GitHub Copilot. And Autopilot is a persistent, proactive and personal agent that keeps working even when you’re not. Home and Code will start rolling out in our Frontier program in the coming weeks and Autopilot is expanding to private preview at the end of the month.

Most tools give you a fixed set of screens and ask you to fit your work into them. But what if you could start with the workflow you want instead and have the interface take shape around it?

That’s the idea behind canvases in the GitHub Copilot app . A canvas, also called a canvas extension, is a customizable interface that you and the agent share. It can be a kanban board, an issue triage board, a release checklist, a dashboard, a form, or even a spreadsheet: a UI shaped to how you work.

paragraphs: For developers and enterprises, model choice is no longer a decision you make at the start of a project.
Ship agents faster with expanded model choice, voice agents, and continuous optimization The best model for your business will keep changing.
Foundry helps teams continuously improve their agents, using production traces to evaluate and refine instructions, skills, tools, and model choice against quality, latency, and cost.
Ship agents faster with expanded model choice, voice agents, and continuous optimization

The best model for your business will keep changing. Adopting it should move your business forward, not send your team back to rebuild the architecture around it. As models advance, organizations need the freedom to choose the right model for each workload, and an agent foundation that can evolve with those choices.

Microsoft Foundry provides that model—and harness—agnostic foundation for building and running agents. Teams can adopt better models as they emerge while preserving their investments in the enterprise systems, knowledge, tools, and controls that make agents useful to their business.

As models advance, organizations need the freedom to choose the right model for each workload, and an agent foundation that can evolve with those choices.

Microsoft Foundry provides that model—and harness—agnostic foundation for building and running agents. Teams can adopt better models as they emerge while preserving their investments in the enterprise systems, knowledge, tools, and controls that make agents useful to their business.

AI is becoming more capable and intuitive — remembering what matters, understanding the world around you, and acting at your direction. Privacy and trust are core to making that possible, ensuring your data stays private and protected as AI systems evolve to provide more continuous assistance across your devices.

Today, we are sharing how we will bring private, server-side memory to our Private AI Compute platform. This breakthrough resolves a longstanding dilemma in modern AI: how to give an assistant long-term continuity across devices while upholding the strict privacy standards typically limited to on-device processing.

sourceContent.headline: Your architecture diagram is not your resilience
sourceContent.description: Learn how the Azure Essentials frameworks, the Well-Architected Framework, and the Cloud Adoption Framework can help you maintain resiliency.
paragraphs: That kept the lights on, but it treated resilience as a project with an end date rather than a property you maintain.
For years, resilience was something you set up once: configure disaster recovery, write a runbook, run the occasional failover test.
Our own incident triage system uses language models to answer which service is responsible for an incident—work that used to mean waking people up to argue over logs.
This first article in our resilience series draws on a conversation with Mark Russinovich about how resilience is changing in the AI era and what it takes to continuously validate it at scale.

What surprises me most about resilience failures is how ordinary the drift is. A workload is deployed across availability zones, but a health probe still points to a single dependency. A database supports failover, but the application’s connection string is pinned to one region. Nothing looks broken. The architecture diagram still shows a resilient design even as the operational reality underneath it changes.

For years, resilience was something you set up once: configure disaster recovery, write a runbook, run the occasional failover test. That kept the lights on, but it treated resilience as a project with an end date rather than a property you maintain.

Our own incident triage system uses language models to answer which service is responsible for an incident—work that used to mean waking people up to argue over logs.

This first article in our resilience series draws on a conversation with Mark Russinovich about how resilience is changing in the AI era and what it takes to continuously validate it at scale.

What surprises me most about resilience failures is how ordinary the drift is. A workload is deployed across availability zones, but a health probe still points to a single dependency. A database supports failover, but the application’s connection string is pinned to one region. Nothing looks broken. The architecture diagram still shows a resilient design even as the operational reality underneath it changes.

For years, resilience was something you set up once: configure disaster recovery, write a runbook, run the occasional failover test. That kept the lights on, but it treated resilience as a project with an end date rather than a property you maintain.

summaryLinesEn: For this illusion to hold, something has to supply the geometry.
Stacked pull requests are a great way to split work into smaller changes, which makes reviews easier and helps teams ship with less risk.

Our diff surface is built around it: An imperative, recycled code-row renderer (no React component per row) An imperative scroll API with exact “scroll to row N “ None of it scales badly, because no per-frame work grows with the total row count.

summaryLinesEn: Engram's setup has one of those screens too, and it takes a couple of minutes to get through: name a project → pick a template → click past topics that are already filled in for you → generate an API key.

articles.descEn: We talk compression and dynamics in the first in a series where we explain the tools behind great-sounding music.
articles.titleEn: What Does a Compressor Actually Do?
summaryLinesEn: A recording of a drum kit will be very dynamic, with loud snare and kick peaks, plus subtle ghost notes and room reverb making up the totality of the sound.
So to understand the compressor, it’s helpful to first look at what we mean by dynamics in the context of audio.
Well, compressed audio is perceived as sounding louder, because the makeup gain is “turning up the quiet” even if the peaks remain the same.

sourceContent.headline: What Does a Compressor Actually Do?
sourceContent.description: We talk compression and dynamics in the first in a series where we explain the tools behind great-sounding music.
paragraphs: A recording of a drum kit will be very dynamic, with loud snare and kick peaks, plus subtle ghost notes and room reverb making up the totality of the sound.
So to understand the compressor, it’s helpful to first look at what we mean by dynamics in the context of audio.
Well, compressed audio is perceived as sounding louder, because the makeup gain is “turning up the quiet” even if the peaks remain the same.

The compressor is one of the most ubiquitous tools used in music production. It is in the family of audio devices known as dynamics processors. So to understand the compressor, it’s helpful to first look at what we mean by dynamics in the context of audio.

Dynamics is the variation of amplitude (sound level) over time. A recording of a drum kit will be very dynamic, with loud snare and kick peaks, plus subtle ghost notes and room reverb making up the totality of the sound. Its dynamic range (the distance between the quietest part and the loudest part) is high. On the other hand, a synth pad — a long ambient texture with little variation in volume — is less dynamic. Its dynamic range is low.

Managing dynamics is important in the music production process, because we need to constantly balance the desire to have a punchy and impressive mix, with the reality that there’s only so much you can cram into your mix before you enter ‘too loud’ territory. So with this baseline understanding of dynamics, back to the compressor.

summaryLinesEn: IDC FinTech Top 100: Solution providers that derive more than one-third of their revenue from the financial services and FinTech industries AND across no more than two additional key non FSI industry verticals.
Firms such as market data providers or credit bureaus that derive revenues from excluded categories, but also have revenue tied to software, hardware, or services, are considered in these rankings.

For these data providers, the revenue attributed to data is used to qualify the provider to the appropriate IDC FinTech category, yet only the qualifying portion of revenue is included in the process.

New framework prioritises faster migration to 4G and 5G, coordinated energy and connectivity investment and more sustainable ways to connect rural communities

21 September, New York: The GSMA and the Partnership for Digital Access in Africa (PDAA) today launched a new roadmap to accelerate meaningful digital participation across Africa and support the ambition of connecting one billion people to the internet by 2030.

Launched during the United Nations General Assembly, Advancing Digital Connectivity in Africa: Charting Africa’s Path to 1 Billion Connected People by 2030 sets out priority actions for governments, industry, development partners and investors to move beyond expanding network coverage and enable more people to use the internet regularly, safely and productively.

sourceContent.headline: Analyzing rising fraud attempts among travel and leisure businesses on Stripe
sourceContent.description: Stripe data shows fraud attempts against travel and leisure businesses hit a four-year high last year. We analyzed payment activity from more than 200,000 businesses on Stripe to understand where fraud is rising and how it’s being blocked.
paragraphs: Trained on more than $1.9 trillion in transaction volume across millions of businesses, Radar blocked more than $3 billion in suspected fraudulent payment volume among travel and leisure merchants last year alone.
Learn more about how AI is changing the fight against fraud , or get in touch to see how Radar can help protect travel revenue.

Fraud attempts are rising in travel and leisure, but successful fraud is declining with Stripe Radar Among Stripe businesses in travel and leisure, fraud attempts rose sharply over the past three years.

For travel and leisure businesses, combating fraud is a balancing act between speed and security. These businesses—which include not only hotels and travel booking platforms, but also museums, theme parks, and live-event venues—sell offerings that are time-sensitive, easily resold, and often purchased across borders. That makes fraudulent transactions hard to stop and losses hard to recover.

At the same time, travelers booking last minute are rarely willing to wait. Travel and leisure businesses need to approve high-value bookings in seconds or risk losing legitimate customers to competitors. As a result, they have less room to add verification steps, even when fraud risk is high.

That’s giving bad actors an opening. Last year, Stripe data shows that fraud attempts against travel and leisure businesses hit a four-year high. We analyzed payment activity from more than 200,000 active travel and leisure businesses on Stripe to understand where fraud is rising, how effectively it’s being blocked, and what businesses can do in response.

articles.title: Digital Reforms Could Connect Over 1 Million More People to Mobile Internet in Rwanda, GSMA Finds
articles.descEn: Affordable smartphones, targeted digital skills programmes and services relevant to everyday life are key to extending digital inclusion among lower-income and rural communities 17 September 2026, Kigali: More than 1 million additional people in Rwanda could be using mobile internet by 2031 through reforms that make smartphones more affordable and digital services more accessible and […]
articles.titleEn: Digital Reforms Could Connect Over 1 Million More People to Mobile Internet in Rwanda, GSMA Finds
summaryLinesEn: Affordable smartphones, targeted digital skills programmes and services relevant to everyday life are key to extending digital inclusion among lower-income and rural communities 17 September 2026, Kigali: More than 1 million additional people in Rwanda could be using mobile internet by 2031 through reforms that make smartphones more affordable and digital services more accessible and relevant to everyday life, according to a new GSMA report released today.

The analysis also finds that increased digital adoption and wider economic activity could more than offset the costs of targeted tax reductions and affordability measures, delivering an estimated net annual fiscal benefit of RWF 218 billion by 2031.

GSMA’s analysis estimates that implementing the recommended reforms could connect approximately 1.07 million additional unique mobile internet subscribers by 2031 – 22.1% more than projected without the reforms.

Affordable smartphones, targeted digital skills programmes and services relevant to everyday life are key to extending digital inclusion among lower-income and rural communities

17 September 2026, Kigali: More than 1 million additional people in Rwanda could be using mobile internet by 2031 through reforms that make smartphones more affordable and digital services more accessible and relevant to everyday life, according to a new GSMA report released today.

The report, Rwanda Digital Economy: Policy reforms that will drive Rwanda’s digital future , calls for targeted action to help lower-income and rural households benefit from the country’s extensive mobile networks. Its recommendations focus on device affordability, digital skills, relevant content and services, and sustainable network investment.

articles.titleEn: What we’ve learned from Microsoft's own AI transformation - The Official Microsoft Blog
summaryLinesEn: We learned that access and usage do not equal transformation: a tool licensed to over 200,000 people does not change how the work gets done.
But when leaders focused on a clear business outcome and what mattered most to the person doing the job, rather than AI adoption itself, conversations shifted from using AI to creating value.
But the ultimate measure is whether AI improves customer and employee experiences, drives growth and innovation, reduces risk and expands what the organization can accomplish.

paragraphs: We learned that access and usage do not equal transformation: a tool licensed to over 200,000 people does not change how the work gets done.
But when leaders focused on a clear business outcome and what mattered most to the person doing the job, rather than AI adoption itself, conversations shifted from using AI to creating value.
But the ultimate measure is whether AI improves customer and employee experiences, drives growth and innovation, reduces risk and expands what the organization can accomplish.
Sep 17, 2026 | Kathleen Hogan - Executive Vice President and Chief Strategy and Transformation Officer

AI is reshaping work faster than any organization has fully mastered. Across industries, the conversation has shifted from what AI can do to how companies can use AI to create business value and expand what people are able to achieve. At Microsoft, we believe the organizations that succeed will be what we call Frontier Firms: human-led, but increasingly AI-enabled. That responsibility begins with how AI is built and continues through how it is put to work: AI should expand human capability while people retain meaningful control, judgment and accountability. We committed to being Customer Zero, learning through our own transformation so we could help others navigate their own.

Our employees have experimented with AI, while leaders have set ambitious goals and challenged teams to reimagine how we work to achieve more than was possible before. We created cross-company councils spanning corporate functions, go-to-market and engineering to share best practices and learn together. We asked everyone to challenge their fixed mindsets and embrace the growth mindset we have cultivated for more than a decade. That work is producing measurable results: for a sales team deal close rates increased by 20% 1 ; selected supply-chain workflows cut cycle time by up to 75% 2 ; and a nine-person engineering team shipped an initial product release in 35 days. 3

articles.titleEn: AlphaGenome Atlas: Molecular predictions for 9 Billion human DNA variants
summaryLinesEn: Today, we are introducing AlphaGenome Atlas: a platform ( detailed in our paper ) containing predictions for the effects of 9 billion single-nucleotide variants — every single-letter change possible — in the human genome.

When we expanded the AlphaFold Database in 2022, we grew the 3D structure information available from around 190K experimental structures to more than 200M structure predictions — covering nearly all catalogued proteins known to science.
By focusing on the 1% of non-coding variants which Atlas predicts to be most impactful, he identified 19 genetic regions, which could help direct the next stage of targeted research into this trait.

paragraphs: Today, we are introducing AlphaGenome Atlas: a platform ( detailed in our paper ) containing predictions for the effects of 9 billion single-nucleotide variants — every single-letter change possible — in the human genome.

How predicting the molecular impact of every possible single-letter DNA variant in the human genome will help accelerate our understanding of biology.

Today, we are introducing AlphaGenome Atlas: a platform ( detailed in our paper ) containing predictions for the effects of 9 billion single-nucleotide variants — every single-letter change possible — in the human genome. It is the most comprehensive catalogue of how genetic mutations affect molecular biology, and it is available for academic research through an intuitive and free-to-use website portal .

DNA is the language of life. Mastering it is a grand challenge that could transform our ability to understand biology and treat disease. But progress has been limited by a fundamental problem: interpreting how genetic variations impact biology at a molecular level. With roughly 9 billion possible single-letter mutations in the human genome, testing each one in the lab is practically impossible.

articles.title: What Stripe data shows about fraud at AI startups
articles.descEn: Here’s a closer look at what our data shows about attempted fraud and multi-account abuse rates at AI companies and how Stripe Radar, our AI-powered fraud prevention product, can help businesses stay ahead of changing fraud patterns.
articles.titleEn: What Stripe data shows about fraud at AI startups
summaryLinesEn: By Q1 2026, AI startups’ attempted fraud rate on Stripe had decreased to 2.6x the rate of startups overall.
As transaction fraud tactics become less likely to succeed, fraudulent actors shift their efforts to other forms of fraud, such as multi-account or free trial abuse.

Radar draws on signals across billions of transactions on the Stripe network to help identify fraudulent payments before a transaction is processed—including cards that have been used fraudulently at other businesses, even when they’re new to yours.

As transaction fraud tactics become less likely to succeed, fraudulent actors shift their efforts to other forms of fraud, such as multi-account or free trial abuse.

Radar draws on signals across billions of transactions on the Stripe network to help identify fraudulent payments before a transaction is processed—including cards that have been used fraudulently at other businesses, even when they’re new to yours.

New Stripe data shows that fraudulent actors disproportionately target AI companies throughout the customer lifecycle. During sign-up, AI subscription companies saw a 40% increase in attempted multi-account abuse in a six-month period. And at the transaction stage, AI startups faced up to 4.3x higher attempted fraud rates than startups overall.
AI founders have recently shared similar experiences on social media.

We also get so much fraud. Very common across most self-serve AI founders I speak with. I vastly underestimated how much fraud and abuse there is on the internet. Stripe has been incredibly helpful at blocking it for us.

articles.titleEn: GSMA warns of emerging global AI divide as three billion people remain offline and smartphone component costs soar
summaryLinesEn: Launching its State of Mobile Internet Connectivity (SOMIC) Report 2026 , the GSMA, which represents the mobile ecosystem worldwide, warns that while artificial intelligence is transforming economies and societies, its benefits will remain out of reach for more than 3.4 billion people who still do not use mobile internet – despite more than 90% of them already living within mobile broadband coverage.

By the end of 2025 an entry-level internet-enabled handset cost the poorest 20% of people in LMICs the equivalent of 44% of their average monthly income , rising to 76% in Sub-Saharan Africa with these costs expected to dramatically rise due to increases in memory costs.

Around 160 million people came online in 2025, down from 190 million the previous year, while 3.1 billion people continue to live within the footprint of mobile broadband networks but do not use mobile internet – the “usage gap”.

15 September 2026, New York : The GSMA today warned that the world risks creating a new global divide between AI “haves” and “have-nots” unless urgent action is taken to address the digital divide and make smartphones affordable for billions of people in low- and middle-income countries.

Launching its State of Mobile Internet Connectivity (SOMIC) Report 2026 , the GSMA, which represents the mobile ecosystem worldwide, warns that while artificial intelligence is transforming economies and societies, its benefits will remain out of reach for more than 3.4 billion people who still do not use mobile internet – despite more than 90% of them already living within mobile broadband coverage. Without affordable smartphones, these people will remain unable to benefit from the AI revolution.

summaryLinesEn: Mobile operators across Asia Pacific purchased or generated 7 TWh of renewable electricity in 2024, equivalent to around 15% of their total electricity consumption – up from just 1% in 2019.

paragraphs: Mobile operators across Asia Pacific purchased or generated 7 TWh of renewable electricity in 2024, equivalent to around 15% of their total electricity consumption – up from just 1% in 2019.

Despite stronger climate commitments by mobile operators across Asia Pacific, emissions in emerging Asian markets have risen by more than 20% since 2019 due to growth in connectivity demand and limited access to renewable energy

10 th September 2026, Kuala Lumpur: Mobile operators across Asia Pacific are making progress towards net zero, but greater access to renewable energy, enabled by energy market reform, is essential to continue on that path, according to the GSMA’s new Mobile Net Zero: Asia Pacific – Regional Focus on Climate Action 2026 report, launched today at M360 ASEAN 2026

Demand for digital connectivity has surged in Asia Pacific, with mobile data traffic up 350% and mobile connections up 6% between 2019 and 2024. Operational emissions in the region rose 6% over the same period, but trends vary significantly between markets. In Southeast Asia, for example, including Malaysia, operator emissions increased by around 20%, driven by growing connectivity demand and network expansion in markets where access to renewables remains a challenge. In Japan and Oceania, operators cut their emissions by more than 30%, thanks to strong progress on renewables.

정부의 경우, 보고서는 분산된 통신 부하에 대한 재생 에너지 조달 및 집합 메커니즘 활성화, 청정 에너지 및 그리드 허가 간소화, 전력 시장 설계 개혁, 석탄 단계적 폐지 가속화를 권장함

articles.title: HFresh: Memory-Efficient Vector Search | Weaviate
articles.descEn: HFresh is Weaviate's disk-based vector index for memory-efficient vector search, combining low heap usage with incremental background maintenance.
articles.titleEn: HFresh: Memory-Efficient Vector Search | Weaviate
summaryLinesEn: HFresh uses: RQ1 for postings , reducing stored vector data by up to 32x compared to 32-bit floats The first stage of HFresh search uses an HNSW index over centroids.
It builds on ideas introduced by the SPFresh research paper, adapting the design to use battle-tested components already present in Weaviate.

Because the centroid layer is only used to identify promising regions of the vector space, HFresh can compress those vectors aggressively enough to reduce memory usage while maintaining the accuracy needed for strong recall.

sourceContent.headline: HFresh: Memory-Efficient Vector Search | Weaviate
sourceContent.description: HFresh is Weaviate's disk-based vector index for memory-efficient vector search, combining low heap usage with incremental background maintenance.
paragraphs: HFresh uses: RQ1 for postings , reducing stored vector data by up to 32x compared to 32-bit floats The first stage of HFresh search uses an HNSW index over centroids.
It builds on ideas introduced by the SPFresh research paper, adapting the design to use battle-tested components already present in Weaviate.

Because the centroid layer is only used to identify promising regions of the vector space, HFresh can compress those vectors aggressively enough to reduce memory usage while maintaining the accuracy needed for strong recall.

HFresh is Weaviate's disk-based vector index for applications that prioritize lower memory use over peak query throughput. That tradeoff is useful for small applications with limited resources as well as large datasets. Weaviate Cloud's Free Tier , for example, uses HFresh by default through its Cost Optimized profile.
Understanding HNSW's memory bottleneck in similarity search ​

When it comes to finding similar vectors quickly, HNSW (Hierarchical Navigable Small World) has become the gold standard. It's fast and accurate, but as datasets grow from millions to billions of vectors, HNSW reveals a fundamental constraint: its graph and vector cache are kept in memory.

summaryLines: HFresh는 게시에 RQ1을 사용하여 저장된 벡터 데이터를 32비트 부동 소수점에 비해 최대 32배까지 줄임 · HFresh 검색의 첫 번째 단계에서는 중심에 대해 HNSW 인덱스를 사용함
이는 SPFresh 연구 논문에서 소개된 아이디어를 바탕으로 Weaviate에 이미 존재하는 전투 테스트를 거친 구성 요소를 사용하도록 디자인을 조정함

Two new GSMA reports launched at today’s M360 ASEAN Digital Trust Summit highlight digital trust as a critical enabler of ASEAN’s digital ambitions and call for coordinated action to strengthen confidence in digital interactions

9 September 2026, Kuala Lumpur: As the Association of Southeast Asian Nations (ASEAN) accelerates its digital economy, AI and digital government ambitions, digital trust is becoming a critical factor in whether citizens, businesses and governments can confidently embrace digital services. Two new GSMA reports launched today at the Digital Trust Summit at M360 ASEAN warn that online scams, fraud and digital deception are increasingly challenging that trust and could undermine progress towards broader digital ambitions.

The first report, the GSMA ASEAN Consumer Scam Report 2026 , found that nearly half (45%) of reported scam cases across Indonesia, Malaysia, the Philippines, Singapore, Thailand and Vietnam remain unresolved despite consumers taking more steps to protect themselves. Consumers with unresolved cases report lower levels of trust in communications channels, digital platforms and data sharing, while many have changed how they engage with digital services and inbound communications.

articles.title: Introducing v6
articles.descEn: A New Generation of Music Models, in Partnership with the Music Industry
articles.titleEn: Introducing v6
summaryLinesEn: This also marks the beginning of a new chapter for music. v6 is designed to expand what is creatively possible and lay the foundation to launch new products that open up revenue opportunities across the music ecosystem.

We’ve also introduced safeguards to screen uploaded audio files and lyrics for unauthorized use, give people greater transparency into how AI is used in music and make it harder for bad actors to abuse these tools.
We started Suno because we believed more people should be able to experience the joy of making music.

sourceContent.headline: Introducing v6
sourceContent.description: A New Generation of Music Models, in Partnership with the Music Industry
paragraphs: This also marks the beginning of a new chapter for music. v6 is designed to expand what is creatively possible and lay the foundation to launch new products that open up revenue opportunities across the music ecosystem.

We’ve also introduced safeguards to screen uploaded audio files and lyrics for unauthorized use, give people greater transparency into how AI is used in music and make it harder for bad actors to abuse these tools.
We started Suno because we believed more people should be able to experience the joy of making music.
Today we’re taking our biggest step yet toward that vision. We’re introducing v6, a new generation of music models developed with our industry partners, including Warner Music Group, BMG and Believe.

v6 models are our best yet. They are faster, more expressive and higher quality, with powerful new features that give creators greater control over their music. v6 brings our most advanced music creation tools to everyone, from Grammy-winning artists to people making their very first song.

articles.title: A New Partnership with Believe and TuneCore
articles.descEn: Working with our industry partners to support a healthy music ecosystem
articles.titleEn: A New Partnership with Believe and TuneCore
summaryLinesEn: Through many candid conversations, we found that we share important values: giving artists meaningful choices and creating more paths to distribution and economic opportunity.

We recently introduced audio watermarking and fingerprinting to help identify Suno songs off-platform and combat fraud and abuse, along with new download limits designed to prevent mass distribution to streaming services.
Today, we’re announcing a global strategic partnership with global artist development company Believe and TuneCore, its platform for self-releasing artists.

Through many candid conversations, we found that we share important values: giving artists meaningful choices and creating more paths to distribution and economic opportunity.

Today, we’re announcing a global strategic partnership with global artist development company Believe and TuneCore, its platform for self-releasing artists.

sourceContent.headline: A New Partnership with Believe and TuneCore
sourceContent.description: Working with our industry partners to support a healthy music ecosystem
paragraphs: Through many candid conversations, we found that we share important values: giving artists meaningful choices and creating more paths to distribution and economic opportunity.

We recently introduced audio watermarking and fingerprinting to help identify Suno songs off-platform and combat fraud and abuse, along with new download limits designed to prevent mass distribution to streaming services.
Today, we’re announcing a global strategic partnership with global artist development company Believe and TuneCore, its platform for self-releasing artists.

Independent artists have always been central to Suno. They are often the first to experiment with new creative tools, and we want to help give them more ways to create, reach audiences and grow their careers.

Today, we’re announcing a global strategic partnership with global artist development company Believe and TuneCore, its platform for self-releasing artists. Believe supports independent artists and labels around the world, helping them develop their careers, while retaining creative independence, sharing their music through platforms like Spotify, Apple Music, Amazon Music and YouTube, and reaching new audiences worldwide.

Believe will be part of the new music models we are developing with the music industry. Together, we’ll create new product experiences that Believe and TuneCore artists can choose to participate in, giving them new ways to collaborate with fans and get paid for their work.

As we enter the next era , what will be the defining measure of our progress?

Every industry has a word that shapes how it thinks. For pilots, it’s safety. For insurers, it’s risk.

If you have ever tried to put a stack of investor decks, scientific papers, or annual reports through a RAG pipeline, then you know the drill: set up an Optical Character Recognition (OCR) or text-extraction step, pick a chunking strategy, embed text, and finally retrieve information. articles.title: MiniMax Launches Revenue Generation via External Partner Collaborations
articles.descEn: MiniMax, a prominent Chinese artificial intelligence startup, has reportedly pivoted to a more lucrative business model that outperforms the profitability of its in-house product development efforts. As a key player in the competitive AI industry, MiniMax’s strategic shift away from standalone product creation marks a notable transformation in its operational roadmap, unlocking higher revenue potential and reshaping its market positioning amid the fast-evolving global AI landscape.
articles.titleEn: MiniMax Launches Revenue Generation via External Partner Collaborations
summaryLinesEn: Revenue from the open platform and other AI enterprise services hit 73.93 million U.S. dollars, accounting for 63.4% of the total revenue; revenue from AI-native products reached 42.64 million U.S. dollars, with the proportion dropping to 36.6%.
MiniMax's first half-year financial report after going public, the most interesting figure is by no means its revenue.
In the same period last year, revenue from AI-native products accounted for 69.7% of MiniMax's total revenue.

articles.title: Agentic Commerce: Your Customers May Not Be Coming To You.
articles.descEn: Many are still investing in their customer channels. Very few ask what happens when an AI agent answered the question and completed the transaction somewhere else.
articles.titleEn: Agentic Commerce: Your Customers May Not Be Coming To You.
summaryLinesEn: In others it is still the phone, and younger customers will not pick one up.
The other thing that survives is the set of interactions you deliberately decline to automate, and the instinct to treat every contact as cost is what destroys it.
For thirty years digital strategy rested on an assumption nobody bothered to write down.

articles.title: Retail Media Report 2026
articles.descEn: Learn which retail media networks and advertisers are winning online attention. Dive into stats on impression share, market trends, category split, & more.
articles.titleEn: Retail Media Report 2026
summaryLinesEn: While total retail media impressions in the US declined 17% in H1 ‘26, home retailers shone as a bright spot.
Heavy hitters like Walmart and Target also saw ad impressions sink, reflecting shifting priorities for general merchandisers in the retail media network space.

Outlets like Lowe’s and Home Depot were able to raise their year-over-year impressions 151% and 43%, respectively — while Amazon, which accounts for 60% of the domestic retail media market, saw a 16% shrinkage in impressions.

summaryLinesEn: That new round brings the company’s total funding to $350 million and gives the startup a valuation of $2.5 billion.

articles.title: Google's Gemini 3.5 Transcribe turns speech to text in 85 languages while auto-correcting your verbal stumbles
articles.descEn: Google's new Gemini 3.5 Transcribe recognizes over 85 languages, strips filler words, and corrects slips of the tongue in real time. It hits a 4.0 percent word error rate in streaming mode, with 70 percent lower latency than its predecessor, Chirp 3. Through function calling, the model can hand off tasks to other Gemini models.
articles.titleEn: Google's Gemini 3.5 Transcribe turns speech to text in 85 languages while auto-correcting your verbal stumbles
summaryLinesEn: Google reports a word error rate of 4.0 percent for streaming and 2.6 percent for recorded audio, with 70 percent lower latency than its predecessor, Chirp 3.
Google has launched Gemini 3.5 Transcribe, a speech-to-text model for real-time transcription.
It's already built into Gboard for Android (via " Rambler ") and the Gemini app on macOS , with Chrome support coming soon.

articles.title: Claude Cowork now runs its own browser inside the desktop app
articles.descEn: Anthropic is building its own browser into Claude Cowork, running inside the desktop app.
articles.titleEn: Claude Cowork now runs its own browser inside the desktop app
summaryLinesEn: When a task needs a website, a browser opens in the side panel, where Claude loads pages, reads them, clicks, and types.
Anthropic is building its own browser into Claude Cowork, running inside the desktop app.
The browser stays separate from your own, so Claude can't see your tabs, bookmarks, or passwords.

articles.title: Bill Gates issues stark warning about AI and the future of humanity - SiliconANGLE
articles.descEn: Bill Gates issues stark warning about AI and the future of humanity - SiliconANGLE
articles.titleEn: Bill Gates issues stark warning about AI and the future of humanity - SiliconANGLE
summaryLinesEn: “We have to think now about how to reduce job losses so that everyone can share in the prosperity that AI creates,” he said.
Gates (pictured), now a philanthropist, said in an almost-6,000-word essay Tuesday that the transition to the AI era will be one of the “most turbulent times in human history.”

AI can be a force for good, he expects, in many areas such as education, agriculture, combatting climate change and improving health systems, but he worries that if the impact people experience is only the massive loss of jobs, then AI optimism will become AI despair.

localization.title: 빌 게이츠, AI와 인류의 미래에 대해 강력히 경고 - SiliconANGLE
summaryLines: 그는 “AI가 창출하는 번영을 모든 사람이 공유할 수 있도록 일자리 손실을 줄이는 방법에 대해 이제 고민해야 한다”고 말함
현재 자선가인 게이츠(사진)는 화요일 약 6000자 분량의 에세이에서 AI 시대로의 전환이 “인류 역사상 가장 격동의 시기” 중 하나가 될 것이라고 말함
그는 AI가 교육, 농업, 기후 변화 퇴치, 의료 시스템 개선 등 다양한 분야에서 선을 위한 힘이 될 수 있다고 기대하지만, 사람들이 경험하는 영향이 막대한 일자리 손실에 불과하다면 AI 낙관론은 AI 절망이 될 것이라고 우려함

articles.titleEn: Z.ai open-sources ‘Ox Alpha’ model as GLM-5.3-Flash - SiliconANGLE
summaryLinesEn: Users requests can include a 1 million tokens worth of text, images and video while GLM-5.3-Flash’s responses contain up to 131,072 tokens.
LLM marketplace operator OpenRouter Inc. launched a free hosted version of Ox Alpha and didn’t disclose its developer, which drew a significant amount of industry attention.
Z.ai Co. today released the code for GLM-5.3-Flash, a large language model that’s 10 times more cost-efficient than its predecessor.

articles.title: Nvidia snaps up Hugging Face for $12.9 billion as closed AI labs pull away
articles.descEn: Nvidia is buying open-source AI platform Hugging Face for $12.9 billion, about 80 times its $150 million annual revenue. The deal fits Nvidia's push to invest billions in open AI models while closed providers like OpenAI and Anthropic move away from Nvidia hardware.
articles.titleEn: Nvidia snaps up Hugging Face for $12.9 billion as closed AI labs pull away
summaryLinesEn: Nvidia is acquiring open-source AI platform Hugging Face for $12.9 billion , according to The Information .
Nvidia previously committed $26 billion over five years to develop open-source AI models.
Nvidia could scale up Hugging Face's cloud business and position it as a kind of OpenRouter for open-weight models.
